- **Pattern:** **A readout's detection score and its predictive score are two different measurements of the same probe, and the folder has now seen them disagree by more than 0.45 in three separate papers: here one linear direction separates clean from corrupted context at 0.985-0.994 AUROC and predicts whether the error reaches the final answer at 0.47-0.53, on matched pairs that differ only in the injected hop value, with both targets scored from the identical probe at the identical layer.** Read against run 917 (a 0.953-AUROC error probe whose four interventions all returned nothing) and run 922 (a 0.953 probe beside a 0.429 behavioural flip rate), the recurrence is sharper than "correlation is not causation": **the folder keeps letting one high number stand for two questions - "is the thing there" and "does it matter" - and the cheap separation is to define both targets before any probe is trained, then print them in the same row.** Mechanical rule for us: **every probe in our white-box model carries two AUROCs in one table cell - detect (the state we claim it reads) and predict (the outcome we say it forecasts), computed on matched pairs where only the claimed quantity differs - and a probe whose predict row is within chance of 0.5 is filed as a state detector and barred from any monitoring or selection claim, however high its detect row; the matched-pair construction is the load-bearing part, because a predict target defined on unmatched inputs just re-measures difficulty.** The paper's own honest supplement is that this survives the controls that would have killed a cheaper claim: grouped folds holding out whole base problems move detection by at most 0.003, and leave-one-error-type-out transfer stays above 0.91 everywhere, so the dissociation is not a leakage artefact - which means the dissociation is the finding, not a failure of the measurement.
- **Pattern:** **A pooling choice can manufacture or hide the depth story, and the paper's own ablation is the cleanest evidence in the folder: under last-token pooling the layer-0 probe is exactly 0.500 and a single first block contributes about 0.38-0.41 AUROC, while the same probe under mean pooling already reads roughly 0.91 at layer 0 because the corrupted operand is smeared across positions by averaging - so "where the signal lives" in this entry is a statement about the aggregation, not only about the network.** Read against run 922 (a probe reaching 1.000 at layer 3 one token position later, filed as a stimulus property) and run 919 (a random split on slow-mixing stimuli manufacturing headroom), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps reporting a layer-resolved peak without reporting the aggregation or the analysis position that produced it, and the two design choices that most often decide the answer - where in the sequence you read, and how you summarise the tokens you read over - are exactly the two the prose tends to leave in a methods paragraph.** Mechanical rule for us: **every layer-resolved readout enters with its aggregation named, both aggregations reported at the earliest layers as well as the peak, and the earliest-saturation layer printed; where mean pooling saturates at the input the entry states that the signal is distributed across tokens rather than localised at the decision point, and the last-token readout is the one used for any information-flow claim, because it is the one that answers "what had the network computed here".** The companion detail worth stealing is the claim that a single block buys about 0.39 AUROC, with the mechanism left open between an attention head spotting an inconsistent token and an MLP feature - the paper says plainly that it does not know which, and that honesty is what makes the number usable as a target for dissection later.

- **Pattern:** **"A cheap state carries it too" is only a finding when the expensive comparator is given the same budget, and this paper's matched-width control is the cleanest published version: one router layer reads the behaviour at 0.608 macro-F1, nine concatenated router layers at 0.659, the best residual layer at 0.658, and residual states from those same nine layers compressed to the same 1,152 dimensions at 0.657 - so parity survives a control that removes both the width and the coverage explanation, and the paired interval is printed beside it.** Read against run 920 (a meta-neuron "beating" SAE features until a joint probe over 20 of those features matched it) and run 918 (an intervention claim that needed its displaced share printed before it could be a cross-model statement), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps accepting a small readout's parity with a large one without matching the two on capacity, coverage or tuning budget, and parity is the claim most easily manufactured by giving the big readout one extra advantage of scale.** Mechanical rule for us: **any claim that a narrow state (a router, a probe, a compressed dictionary, a single direction) matches a wider one is reported with a width-matched and coverage-matched comparator built from the wider state's own features, the paired interval on the difference, and the wide readout's width ratio - and where the matched comparator closes the gap the claim is recorded as "the narrow state loses nothing at this width", never as "the narrow state is sufficient".** The paper's own honest tail is the width ratio itself: parity at 56% of the residual probe's width is still a loss of 44% to a readout that costs nothing at inference.
- **Pattern:** **A cross-domain association score must subtract each domain's own baseline before it can be read as behaviour, and the permutation null has to be drawn inside the trace rather than across the corpus - here the dataset-relative risk difference plus a within-trace label shuffle separates a 0.729 same-behaviour profile correlation from a -0.107 different-behaviour one, and a 0.511 cross-dataset Jaccard from a 0.202 null, while the transfer AUC is left to fall where it falls (0.768 overall but 0.631 for execution, the behaviour most entangled with doing the maths itself).** Read against run 918 (a ranking criterion that could only express the shape its ruler could express) and run 915 (own-slice need versus mixed need, where the aggregate hid the transfer), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps reporting a component-behaviour association computed over a corpus in which the behaviours are unevenly distributed across domains, so "this component is for X" and "this corpus uses X more when it is doing Y" are indistinguishable until the baseline is subtracted and the null is shuffled within the unit that carries the confound.** Mechanical rule for us: **every association our white-box model reports between a component and a label is computed relative to the label's own baseline rate in that material, the null permutes labels within the smallest unit that preserves the confound (here the trace, preserving trace membership and label counts), and the transfer number is reported per class rather than pooled, because the pooled 0.768 hides an execution row at 0.631 that says the association is partly the task.**

(1) **The first-answer cut as a locality instrument**: split each trace at the point where the model already has the answer, steer only one side, and report the trace length before the cut (422 against 441 tokens) beside the length after it - it converts "the edit shortens the trace" into "the edit acts on post-answer computation", which no aggregate token count can. Its companion is the same-seed regeneration at a real stage boundary, which shows what the model does *instead* (wrap-ups 68 against new angles 11, versus 23 against 23 unmodified) rather than only what it stops. (2) **The release experiment as the test that an effect is sustained rather than triggered**: suppressing planning for one window still tilts the next plan toward wrapping up (43 against 21) but barely changes how often thinking ends (6% against 5%), because the postponed check returns once suppression lifts - a done/undone contrast that separates a redirect from a reminder and would be cheap to run on any of our own interventions. - **Pattern:** **A readout is only as meaningful as the ceiling you compare it to, and this paper's whole argument is built from theory-computed ceilings rather than a null: belief states are decodable at 0.83-0.99, which says little alone, but the surplus over next-token probabilities correlates 0.85-1.00 with the surplus the HMM's emission matrix leaves available, the surplus over an order-one approximation correlates 0.59-0.86, and the one family where the theory says there is nothing to detect (Mess3, invertible emission) shows nothing - so the evidence is not that the number is high but that the number is the size the process predicts.** Read against run 918 (a displaced-share swing of 0.12-0.27 across a model ladder that turns a fixed coefficient into a manufactured scaling law) and run 914 (a mining-fold AUROC of 0.998 that says nothing about held-out transfer), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps comparing a readout to a null when the informative comparison is to the ceiling the simplest competing explanation can reach, and a null can only ever prove that the readout found *something*.** Mechanical rule for us: **every readout in our white-box model is reported as a triple - observed, floor (shuffled/random), and ceiling (what the nearest simpler candidate representation alone could achieve) - and the claim we make is about where the observed value sits between floor and ceiling, not about its distance from the floor; where the ceiling is near the observed value the readout is recorded as non-diagnostic for that quantity, and a planned battery includes at least one probe the theory says must fail, because a design that can only succeed is not a test.**
- **Pattern:** **A random train/test split on slow-mixing stimuli reports headroom that a causally honest split removes, and the paper catches itself doing it: across 240 model-process combinations the median peak R-squared is 0.986 under the random split, 0.970 under a contiguous block and 0.976 under held-out sequences, but in the Arch family - the highest-entropy, slowest-mixing one - the parameter trend is invisible under the random split and monotone under both honest ones, with Qwen3.5-9B falling from 0.88 to 0.64 at the top of the sweep.** Read against run 915 (own-slice need versus mixed need, where the aggregate hid the transfer) and run 913 (a level R-squared of 0.53-0.77 against a delta R-squared of 0.10), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps fitting readouts on correlated material with a split that lets adjacent training points bracket the test point, and here the paper prints both readings and shows the trend lives in the difference.** Mechanical rule for us: **any readout fitted on temporally ordered or otherwise correlated inputs - token positions, rollout steps, neighbouring prompts - is reported under a contiguous or held-out-unit split beside the random-split number, and the drop between them is the reported quantity; a random split on correlated data is recorded as an upper bound, not as the result.** Their own failure mode is worth copying as a caveat: they name the mechanism (slow mixing means a contiguous block visits only part of the geometry, so 1,000 fit positions do not cover it) and then say plainly that they have not tested it.

- **Pattern:** **A scaling law can be manufactured by the unit of intervention alone, and this paper prints the miscalibration: the share of the residual that a raw steering injection displaces swings between 0.12 and 0.27 across the Qwen3 ladder with no clean relation to size, so a fixed raw coefficient is a different intervention in every model - and under those raw units the effect rises monotonically with scale in exactly the shape one would report as an emergent capability.** Read against run 917 (a 0.953-AUROC probe with four interventions returning nothing) and run 916 (a correlation of 0.87-0.92 across relations that only survives while nobody partials it out), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps reading a cross-model trend as a property of the models, when a cross-model comparison requires first showing that the intervention was the same size in each model, and no steering paper in this folder has printed that quantity.** Mechanical rule for us: **every cross-model or cross-layer comparison our white-box model makes prints the intervention's displaced share of the residual (or its equivalent natural scale) beside the effect, and where that share varies by more than a small band across the compared units the comparison is reported as between interventions and not between models - the normalised arm is the only one allowed a trend claim, and its slope is printed with its interval.** The companion quantities here are the pass-rate (grid-sensitive, secondary) and the continuous specificity effect (primary), reported together, which is the right way round.

- **Pattern:** **Which units get ranked decides which structure gets found, and the flipped dissection is the cleanest instance in the folder: neuron tuning ranked by linear correlation with the number can only return monotonic units, so "no bell-shaped number neurons" was a property of the ruler, and a shape-agnostic held-out quadratic fit finds them in every model - common in the top thirty for Llama, Phi and Mistral, rare or absent for Qwen; the same effect flips a language dissociation, where gradient-times-activation ranks Chinese as robustly selective in all seventeen models while activation magnitude makes English significant in 7 of 9 and breaks two Qwen.** Read against run 914 (a mined abstention feature at 0.998 AUROC whose identity is stable across seeds but whose held-out transfer is source-specific) and run 917 (a probe excellent as a predictor and worthless as a lever), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps treating a screen as a discovery, when a screen with a linear criterion, a top-k budget or one importance score can only re-find its own criterion, and the honest report of a screen is the criterion plus the second criterion that would have found something else.** Mechanical rule for us: **every ranked list our white-box model publishes - neurons, features, directions, concepts - is produced twice under two different ranking criteria, the overlap and the disagreements are printed, and any claim about a *shape* of representation is made only from a criterion that can express that shape; a single-criterion ranking is recorded as a screen.** The paper's own warning about the top thirty is the size of the budget problem: bell units were common in three families among the top thirty and rare among Qwen's, so the top-k cut is doing a lot of the work.

- **What we take from it (recorded, no extra pattern).** Three copy-ready pieces. (1) The **relabelling construction**: draw a random bijection from a known relation's answers to a fresh label set, fine-tune on a subset of subjects under a fictional frame, and test held-out subjects that share an answer with training ones - it manufactures a genuinely new relation whose structure is inherited, so only the representation can supply the transfer, and it needs no probing of the fine-tuned model at all. (2) The **fixed-in-advance probe**: PCA to 16 dimensions plus whitening, ridge at 10^-2, layer picked by an inner loop only, all frozen before any relation is seen - the cheapest defence against the folder's recurring "the probe was tuned to the outcome" objection, and worth adopting verbatim at our sample sizes. (3) The **subject-broken shuffle** as the null for any attribution: redistribute a model's wrong answers among its own errors so the output preferences are preserved and only the stimulus link is broken, computed as an exact expectation rather than by sampling, with a separate uniform-chance baseline for explanations a shuffle cannot test (the most-frequent-answer row rises to 6.1% from 5.0% under shuffle, which is the paper honestly showing its own null behaving as theory predicts).

- **Pattern:** **A guarantee can be bought by constraining the model to satisfy the assumption that produces it, and this paper's objective does exactly that plus a threshold that hides the cost: the anchor condition is what makes the factorization unique, and it is not tested but *imposed* as a differentiable constraint during training, with the anchor score required to reach τ = 0.99 per factor while model selection only keeps runs that reached constraint feasibility.** Read against run 904 (a faithfulness certificate whose guarantee died at exactly the retention that made it usable) and run 910 (a decomposition certified additive while a placebo absorbed 36.2%), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps reading an assurance about a decomposition as a property of the system, when the assurance is conditional on a structural assumption the method is free to install.** Mechanical rule for us: **every identifiability or fidelity claim our white-box model makes names the assumption it rests on and reports that assumption's measured status in the same row - how often it holds unconstrained, and its value on the fitted solution - and a method that enforces the assumption during fitting reports the share of the guarantee that survives when the constraint is dropped, because an imposed anchor certifies that the recovered object is anchored, not that the system had anchors.**
- **Pattern:** **An identifiability theorem gives a coordinate system, not a name, and the paper's own real-system table shows the size of the gap: a factor correlates 0.80 (Pearson) with divisibility by 2 and 0.88 RDC, while the concept the task actually turns on - divisibility by 3 - reaches 0.058 Pearson (0.32 RDC) and the digit sum 0.110 (0.158), so the mechanism the authors' own intuitive account of the task requires is recovered roughly as well as a random control (0.1416 RDC for divisibility by 5).** Read against run 900 (a feature label that predicted nothing about behaviour) and run 899 (a screen significant on 255 latents where 68% tested were flat), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps treating "we recovered the concept" and "we recovered the concept the system uses" as the same finding, and here the two separate inside a single table by a factor of nearly three.** Mechanical rule for us: **for every component our white-box model nominates, the report carries the score against the concept the behavioural account requires (the mechanism we believe the model implements), not only against the concept that scores highest - and where that required concept lands near the negative-control band, the component is recorded as "found something" rather than "found the mechanism", with the control band printed beside it.** Their negative-concept arm is the instrument: three irrelevant primes at 0.066 MCC-RDC set the floor that the real concepts must clear, and it is the only number in the table that makes the 0.72 headline interpretable.
- **What we take from it (recorded, no extra pattern).** Three copy-ready pieces. (1) The anchor diagnostic as a structural distinctness test: a variable whose only child (only parent) is the factor, checked as minimal rows/columns of the adjacency matrix - the same distinctness question runs 906 and 908 asked behaviourally, here at the level of one structural check per factor. (2) The layered acyclicity constraint, O(nm + mL) per step, which turns the expensive general DAG constraint into a computation nearly free for any block-structured network and rules out a whole class of impossible high-level solutions. (3) Theorem 4's bound: an approximate-transformation error bounded linearly in the training objective when the mechanisms are Lipschitz, proof by nilpotency of the factor-level adjacency, which is the cleanest statement the folder has that a lower loss is a certificate of a closer abstraction rather than merely a better fit. Their state map and their parametric intervention map (which replaces the intervened variables' mechanisms *inside* the factor's own mechanism, rather than overwriting the factor) are the correct formal shapes for the intervention translation our model needs.

- **Pattern:** **A targeted ablation is not targeted, and this paper prints the number that makes it undeniable: in all three main models the per-source maximum collateral effect equals or exceeds the source's own self-effect (Llama 4.61 against 4.06, Gemma 5.11 against 5.03, Mistral 3.20 against 3.11), while the aggregate selectivity ratio is 1.13 at rank 2 and 0.82 at rank 3 - so there is always at least one other behaviour damaged at least as much as the one being edited, and adding rank buys no extra reach on the target while pushing the ratio below one.** Read against run 908 (a content-free random push reproducing a whole collateral ordering at rank correlation 0.90) and run 909 (a matched-direction control that learned to invert its own edit), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps reporting the diagonal of an intervention as its effect, when the off-diagonal of the same matrix is what decides whether the edit was an edit or a perturbation.** Mechanical rule for us: **every intervention our white-box model proposes is reported with its full cross-effect matrix over tracked behaviours, the diagonal, the mean and maximum off-diagonal, and the selectivity ratio, in one row; a proposed edit whose max collateral meets or exceeds its self-effect is filed as a perturbation of the shared representation, not as a control on the target.** The corollary the paper supplies is the rank trade: selectivity 1.75 at rank 1, 1.13 at rank 2, 0.82 at rank 3 - the dimension that makes a subspace expressive is also the dimension that makes it shared.
- **Pattern:** **Overlap is a gate, not a dose, and the paper's own correlation table shows how little of the effect it accounts for: the pooled unnormalised Pearson correlation between residualised subspace overlap and cross-effect magnitude is +0.050 with a confidence interval spanning zero, only Llama reaches +0.430, Gemma sits at +0.164 with the CI lower end at +0.03 - and yet a random rank-2 subspace produces effects 147x to 319x smaller, so the null certifies that the extracted subspace is doing something while the correlation says overlap does not tell you how much.** Read against run 910 (a disentanglement score at 1.000 carrying a mid-range effect share) and run 903 (a headline score ranking below its own baseline), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps treating a spectacular null gap as validation of the object rather than as validation of the procedure - a 300x gap over random proves the subspace is not random, and it is compatible with the geometry being almost irrelevant to effect size.** Mechanical rule for us: **a null baseline in our reports is only accepted as evidence of relevance if the effect-versus-predicted relationship is reported in the same table with its interval; when the interval spans zero the null is recorded as having ruled out generic projection and nothing more, and the explanatory variable is demoted to a regime indicator (which pairs can interact) rather than a magnitude predictor.** Their residualisation is the instrument to keep: projecting out the two decision-correlated PCs before measuring overlap removes the shared axis that makes every behaviour look alike, and the same step is what turns raw overlap into a usable, heterogeneous geometry.
- **What we take from it (recorded, no extra pattern).** The shared/private split (both subspaces' bases, the alignment matrix, singular directions with σ ≥ 0.5 as "shared", each private basis being the residual after removing the shared directions) is the cheapest test the folder has for whether two of our components share a mechanism or merely co-fire, and its Gemma Deceptive/Malicious-NSFW row is the honest failure mode: when both principal directions are shared (k = 2), removing the shared part costs about as much as removing the private parts (-1.26 / -1.18 versus -1.14, -1.13 / -1.13, -1.12), which is why the authors explain orthogonality constraints failing to remove side effects. The three prompt templates (learn-comply, learn-refuse, eval) with the explicit log-prob REFUSE-vs-COMPLY margin are a copy-ready contrastive harness, and the bootstrap refit of the *entire* pipeline - not just the PCA - is the stability protocol worth reusing.

- **Pattern:** **An independence criterion satisfied to a residual of zero is not evidence that each concept carries its share, and the paper prints the loss that turns the check into a trap: with sufficiency plus independence alone the active share reaches 98.0%, *above* the 97.3% of the full four-term model, yet a placebo concept added to the ontology absorbs 36.2% of the effect and a single scalar slot recovers only 69.9%.** Read against run 906 (a three-mechanism mixture whose least distinct member could be deleted for free) and run 904 (a certificate that only holds at near-total retention), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps accepting an additive or complete decomposition as proof that every named part is load-bearing, when both additivity and completeness are properties of the sum.** Mechanical rule for us: **every component decomposition our white-box model reports is run with a hand-added placebo component and a pooled variant of two real components in the same table, and the reported share of each real component is the value *after* the placebo arm is subtracted or the placebo is reported beside it; a decomposition where the placebo earns a non-trivial share is filed as a decomposition of the output, not as an account of which concepts matter.** The corollary the paper supplies is the second half: the diagonal check (each slot against its own counterfactual) and the sum check (contributions adding up) are separate requirements, and only a training-time term enforces the diagonal.
- **Pattern:** **A concept-accuracy score, a disentanglement score and a causal effect share are three different measurements that can all point at different models, and this paper's two dissociation rows are the cleanest version in the folder: iVAE reaches DCI disentanglement 1.000 with active-concept effect share 47.6%, while a model at only 0.914 disentanglement routes 75.3% - and injecting 10% label noise costs the active share 97.3% to 71.6% on aircraft control while concept accuracy holds at 96.2% against 96.4%.** Read against run 903 (a headline score ranking below its own baseline) and run 900 (a feature label that predicted nothing about behaviour), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps using a representational quality score as a proxy for a functional one, and here the proxy is not merely noisy but systematically misleading at both ends of its range.** Mechanical rule for us: **whenever we report a representational score for a component, the same row carries its effect share under our own interventional measure and the correlation between the two across the models we have, and a score whose top value coincides with a mid-range effect share is recorded as measuring something else; label-quality stress (10% noise) belongs in the standard reporting block, since it moves the causal measure by ~26 points while leaving the accuracy score flat.**
- **What we take from it (recorded, no extra pattern).** Two instruments: the frozen-backbone wrapper with a bias-free value projection makes a *zero* concept a legitimate counterfactual reference (the zeroed slot contributes exactly zero value while keeping positive attention weight), which removes the usual objection that zero is off-manifold — the same construction is copy-ready for any attention-style aggregation we build. And the train-with-a-model / evaluate-without-it discipline: the flow and the training losses are used only during fitting, while every reported effect comes from a Shapley-matched estimator over held-out pairs that uses neither.

- **Pattern:** **A statistic that is near-perfectly reliable can be uncorrelated with a perfectly reliable effect - and the paper prints both reliabilities side by side: the structural self-cosine reproduces across halves at 0.982-0.997 in all five models measured, while the behavioural per-head effect reproduces at only 0.419-0.795 and, at Pythia-2.8B, the raw correlation between them is +0.003 with an effect reliability of 0.632.** Read against run 903 (a headline score ranking below its own baseline) and run 892's line of rank-versus-effect reversals, the recurrence is that **the folder keeps quoting a correlation between a computed statistic and a downstream effect without ever asking whether either measurement is reproducible at the granularity it is computed on** - and here the answer is asymmetric: the representation-side statistic is essentially noise-free while the intervention-side effect, measured one head at a time on 64 documents, is attenuated enough that the authors must divide the raw correlation by a reliability factor just to see the association (0.149 raw to 0.231 adjusted, and a Pythia-1.4B value of 0.187 to 0.232). Mechanical rule for us: **every rank correlation between a representation statistic and an effect our white-box model reports carries a split-half reliability for each side and the resolution verdict, and when the effect side lands in the attenuated band the entry states that the correlation is floor-limited by measurement, not by absence of association** - because 0.419 on the effect side caps the observable raw correlation regardless of the truth. The corollary is the ascending-threshold discipline: they classify rather than test, so an unresolvable effect (r_Δ < 0.3) is reported as unresolvable instead of as a null result.

- **Pattern:** **A perturbation with no semantic content reproduces the entire collateral ranking of real interventions - and this paper prints the correlation next to the behaviour it cannot produce: a random direction matched only in added norm induces behaviours in the same order as real steers at rank correlation 0.90 (Pearson 0.92 on magnitudes), induces ten behaviours led by the sinks refusal, numeric, poeticism and sycophancy, suppresses seven, and yet produces profanity at exactly 0.0 while inducing toxicity at 0.16.** Read against run 907 (twenty matched-norm random directions spanning 0.16 to 0.58 against a hand-built steer's 0.48) and run 899 (a significance screen significant on 255 latents where 68% tested were flat under clamping), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps measuring an intervention's effect without a content-free twin of the same size, and the two runs that did print the twin both found the headline effect inside the random band - this run is the first where the twin reproduces the effect's entire *ordering* and only fails on the lexically specific behaviours, which is what lets the authors separate "any push drifts here" from "this direction does this thing".** Mechanical rule for us: **every steering result we report is run three ways - the real vector, a matched-norm random vector, and the real vector with all other tracked components projected out - and the report gives the rank correlation between the real and random collateral profiles alongside the specific behaviours the random push cannot produce, because a high correlation means the effect is the model's default and a low one is the only evidence the vector carries content.** The corollary: report collateral as a *ranking over all tracked behaviours*, never as the single named side effect, since the ranking is what the null can be compared against.
- **Pattern:** **Two numbers that cannot express a one-way effect are nonetheless used as its measure, and the paper's split shows how much of the phenomenon such an account is barred from - interference is 0.68 of total magnitude in the antisymmetric part, one pattern inside it carries 0.54, and the geometrically obvious quantity (cosine overlap) predicts that part at best 0.16 and at worst -0.03 over 190 pairs, while acting on the geometry leaves collateral unmoved (-0.03, +0.02) and only weakens the steer it was meant to clean (on-target 2.2 judge points to 1.2 and 1.8).** Read against run 906 (a three-mechanism mixture that fit 0.915-0.995 yet contained a component removable for free) and run 902 (a detector whose held-out advantage collapsed while the repair held), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps testing a proposed explanation only where it is defined, and this run supplies the general instrument: split the effect matrix into the part the explanation's symmetry permits and the part it forbids, and measure the second - whatever sits in the forbidden part is outside the account in principle, not merely poorly fitted.** Mechanical rule for us: **for every account of a component's effect that rests on a symmetric or pairwise quantity (overlap, cosine, mutual information, an undirected attribution rank), the results table also reports the antisymmetric part of the measured effect matrix and the account's held-out score on that part alone; an account whose reach is confined to the symmetric part is filed as descriptive, and an intervention derived from it is reported with its effect on the target and on collateral separately, since removing the overlap here cost most of the intended effect and none of the side effects.** Secondary instrument: leave-one-*group*-out, not leave-one-pair-out - each behaviour appears in 38 pairs, so hiding one pair lets a predictor win by learning general target susceptibility, the exact false positive this run rules out.

The additive entity-times-space test (R-squared 0.92-0.95 with principal cosine 0.29-0.34, stable under fixed, varied and bare base clauses) is a copy-ready composition check. The construction result - a compound space reuses the base slot (0.90 over a 0.03 floor) while minting a router that transfers nothing to its base (0.00, cosine at most 0.26) - is a template for testing whether our own model's composition is reuse-plus-new-index rather than collapse.

- **Pattern:** **A model that covers almost all of behaviour can still contain a component it can drop for free, and this paper prints the pair: the three-mechanism mixture reproduces the empirical pronoun distribution at a Jensen-Shannon similarity between 0.915 and 0.995 in all ten models, while removing group binding from that mixture raises the fit in OLMo-2-13B by 0.022 and leaves it unchanged in several others, and removing recency and stereotype together is what costs the most everywhere.** Read against run 903 (a headline score ranking below its own baseline) and run 904 (a certificate whose guarantee died at exactly the retention that made it useful), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps reading high coverage as evidence that every named component is doing work, when coverage is a property of the union and the ablation is the only test of the parts.** Mechanical rule for us: **every multi-component explanation of our model's output reports its coverage score next to a leave-one-out table, and a component whose removal does not lower coverage is deleted from the explanation rather than listed with a small weight, because a positive weight fitted on a union can live entirely off the other members.** The corollary the paper hands us: their group-binding subspace overlaps the stereotype subspace in the transfer matrix, so the deletable component is also the non-distinct one - distinctness and load-bearing are two tests of the same component and neither substitutes for the other.
- **Pattern:** **Ablating one of two routes that carry the same answer can make the model right, and the table prints the sign: zeroing the top-100 token-copying heads raises pronoun accuracy by 0.44 in Qwen2.5-7B and 0.40 in Llama-3.1-8B, while the same operation in OLMo-2-1B and OLMo-2-7B costs 0.36 - so one intervention on one route moves accuracy in both directions depending on which route was winning.** Read against run 892 (a two-dimensional parasite subspace that passed intervention equivalence by construction) and run 901 (a probe family that failed diagonal dominance - only 18 of 48 ruin checks moved the intended coordinate most), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps attributing an improvement to the component it removed, when the improvement belongs to the removal of competition between components.** Mechanical rule for us: **any ablation whose effect is positive is reported as a reallocation, not an improvement, and the row carries the response of the competing component or route in the same run - an ablation that raises a metric is evidence that two handles exist, not that the ablated unit was harmful, and the paper's own explanation is that suppressing the token route lets the concept route answer.** Secondary instrument worth copying: their token-route probe has no distinct head set at all (OLMo-2-1B needs 72 heads to fall from 0.80 to 0.44), which is what a genuinely distributed mechanism looks like when you look for a local one.
- **What we take from it (recorded, no extra pattern).** The diagnostic-dataset construction (two mechanisms agree on the source, so one intervention isolates the third) is the cheapest attributable-intervention design the folder has, and the authors' reason for preferring it to layer differences - agreeing mechanisms both score well, so a layer gap is only suggestive - is a direct caution on every "the mechanism lives at layer L" claim we make. The frozen-rotation transfer matrix is a copy-ready specificity test. The mixture over per-mechanism intervention softmaxes is a small predictor of an output *distribution* rather than a label, at one forward pass per mechanism per example.

- **Pattern:** **A validity test can be inflated by the very class of variables it is supposed to police, and the inflation is visible in the paper's own power curves: on the unreachable-state experiment the faithfulness-aware CAE converges more slowly and with lower power than its faithfulness-free ablation, because perturbing the unmapped group occasionally pushes the valid system into the same micro-region as the invalid one and raises the valid-condition score, shrinking the gap.** Read against run 899 (a significance screen significant on 255 latents where 68% of tested ones were flat under clamping) and run 904 (an honest certificate that only exists at near-total dictionary retention), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps finding that the instrument which fixes one false claim opens another - here the added test both catches two failures the ablation misses and dulls one the ablation caught cleanly, and the paper prints both directions in the same figure.** Mechanical rule for us: **any faithfulness or completeness test our white-box model adds is reported as a pair of scores on every experiment - with the test and without it - plus a count of cases where adding it reduced specificity, because a test with an unmapped-variable arm has a non-zero chance of making the valid object look invalid and that cost is part of the measurement.** The companion observation: in most of their systems the unmapped group is empty, so the faithful and faithfulness-free rows are the same measurement printed twice, and treating the two rows as independent evidence would manufacture a confirmation.
- **Pattern:** **The cost of proving an explanation wrong is set by how often it is wrong, not by how big the model is, and this paper derives and then measures the law: on Tracr sort-rank transformers grown from length 2 to 15, a high-level model that errs only when the first token is the sequence minimum is detected in about 2.5 times the sequence length interventions at 95% power, matching the analytic prediction, while principled multi-node sampling reaches near-certain separation within thirty interventions on most benchmark systems.** Read against run 897 (a boundary rank correlation turning negative where the global correlation stayed near 0.83) and run 890 (a rank correlation rising while the plans it ranked were unexecutable), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps budgeting its checks by object size and by metric elegance rather than by the rarity of the region where an explanation actually fails.** Mechanical rule for us: **every predictive check we propose carries an estimated sample budget computed from the predicted frequency of the divergence region (one over the probability that the wrong model and the right model disagree on a drawn input), and a check whose divergence region cannot be located is reported as unmeasurable rather than assigned a large budget; a rare systematic error is certifiable, but at a cost proportional to its rarity, and the ratio is part of the claim.** Corollary the benchmark supplies for free: a single-variable sampling scheme misses backup paths and wrong intermediates, so the intervention set must include multi-node interventions and the variables an explanation declares irrelevant.
- **What we take from it (recorded, no extra pattern).** The benchmark's construction pattern - for each system, a hand-built correct abstraction *and* a hand-built near-miss that is observationally identical - is the cheapest way to test any scoring procedure we invent, and it costs a day of work per system. The applicability column (what fraction of the objects a metric is even defined on) is the reporting instrument the folder should print next to every score. Proposition D.1's additive-degradation bound lets us validate a stack of abstractions level by level instead of end to end.

- **Pattern:** **The certificate only holds where the sparse decomposition has stopped compressing, and the paper's own pool ratios say so: non-vacuity is achieved with the calibration pool covering 0.981 to 0.997 of the dictionary, and the frequency-thresholded table on Llama Layer 30 shows the bound climbing as the pool is made selective - retaining only features seen at least 20 times pushes the asymptotic floor from 7.17 to 14.03 bits and 50 times pushes it to 22.14, above the 16.97 baseline, so the guarantee dies before the pool becomes interesting.** Read against run 899 (a significance screen significant on 255 latents where 68% of tested ones were flat under clamping) and run 903 (a headline score ranking below its own baseline), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps finding that the property being certified is bought by giving up the thing the method was for - here the honest bound requires near-total dictionary coverage, which is exactly the regime where the SAE is not selecting anything.** Mechanical rule for us: **any faithfulness or guarantee claim our white-box model makes carries, in the same row, the selectivity of the object it is made about (fraction of the dictionary or activation space retained, or the equivalent sparsity ratio), and a claim that only survives at near-total retention is reported as a statement about the model's output given its own activations rather than about the decomposition.**
- **Pattern:** **A layer can be permanently uninformative regardless of data, and the calculation that shows it costs nothing: the asymptotic floors at Llama layers 4, 8, 12 and 16 are 26.29, 25.24, 19.32 and 17.05 bits, all above the 16.97 uniform baseline, so no evaluation sample size can make those layers certify, while layers 20, 24, 28 and 30 floor at 12.52, 10.72, 10.55 and 7.17 and cross at 450k, 150k, 90k and 10k samples respectively.** Read against run 897 (a surrogate whose boundary rank correlation went negative while global correlation stayed at 0.83, where the paper's remedy was to keep the teacher near the threshold) and run 900 (a feature whose label predicted nothing about its behaviour), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps treating a failing measurement as an expensive measurement, when the failure is structural and cheap to detect.** Mechanical rule for us: **before spending samples on any site in our model, we compute the data-free floor of the quantity we propose to estimate - measured terms held fixed, sample-size corrections set to zero - and a site whose floor cannot beat the naive baseline is reported as structurally uninformative and excluded, with the floor printed; only sites whose floor clears the baseline get a sample budget.**
- **What we take from it (recorded, no extra pattern).** The horizon-conditioned rollout (feed base and reconstructed state through the same h downstream blocks, plot divergence against h) is the cleanest local-fidelity-versus-amplification separator the folder has; the coefficient-to-identity shuffle, which preserves values, support size and pool size exactly, is a one-line null that rules out "fidelity is just activation statistics"; and the decomposition itself - subtract the proxy's own risk, charge the rest to named terms - is the reporting shape to adopt for every component we nominate.

- **Pattern:** **The headline score is the weakest signal in its own table, and the paper prints both rows: MeanRSS alone ranks recurrent failure at AUROC 0.526 and 0.506 on the two probes, below plain clean margin at 0.863 and 0.901, while the same support's erosion subtracted from the full clean margin reaches 0.935 and 0.958 - so the thing that wins the representation study contributes mostly by explaining part of an already-good baseline rather than by working as a detector on its own.** Read against run 899 (a significance screen significant on 255 latents where 68% of tested ones were flat under clamping) and run 902 (a detector whose advantage collapsed out of family while its repair held), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps promoting the score that its selection procedure was built to maximise, and this entry is the first where the promoted score is measured as a standalone risk signal in the same table that shows the residual construction doing the work.** Mechanical rule for us: **no score our white-box model introduces is reported on its own; it is reported as (a) standalone AUROC, (b) as a correction added to the current best baseline, and (c) the baseline alone, with all three in one row, and a score whose standalone value sits below the baseline is described as a decomposition of the baseline rather than as a predictor.** The corollary the paper supplies: the mismatched-control arm (a support selected for a different transformation) is the honest floor - 0.326 versus 0.430 retention - and is more informative than the random arm (0.014), which only rules out "any twenty features".

- **What we take from it (recorded, no extra pattern).** The residual-margin construction (keep the strongest existing score, credit a component only by what it adds) is the reporting shape our predictive model should adopt for every nominated component. The selection/evaluation split over *realizations of the same operators* (5 to select, 10 to evaluate, no operator held back) is the cheaper of their two persistence tests and is worth reusing when the variant family is large.

- **Pattern:** **The same decomposition scores near-perfect or broken depending only on how hard the ablation is searched for, and the paper prints that axis as a table: KL divergence to the target model is 0.828 at 20 PGD steps, 1.354 at 40, 3.838 at 80, 25.256 at 160 and 40.220 at 320, against about 67.24 for zero-ablating every weight matrix - so 160 steps of a cheap attacker already gets roughly a third of the way to total destruction on a decomposition whose authors describe it as mechanistically faithful.** Read against run 888 (a floor fixed by construction rather than estimated) and run 892 (an intervention-equivalence certificate satisfiable by construction), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps certifying faithfulness against a baseline it chose, and this entry is the first where the certificate's strength is an explicit knob with the whole sweep printed.** Mechanical rule for us: **every faithfulness, sparsity or sufficiency number in our reports carries the ablation regime that produced it (random masks, importance-derived masks, or an optimised attacker with its step count and learning rate), and an optimised-attack column is mandatory rather than optional - a component set that survives random masking and collapses at 160 steps is described as sufficient for the average ablation, never as faithful.**
- **Pattern:** **Sufficiency and coverage come apart on one candidate set and the gap is measured by the same attacker: six subcomponents reproduce the gendered-pronoun prediction better than the model does (0.895 under importance masking against 0.586), transfer to a reworded prompt, and drop the prediction below 0.0005 when attacked, while the 150-subcomponent graph that is actually adversarially pruned still loses the target from 0.586 to 0.443 - so neither set is the computation, and the larger one is 25 times the size while remaining incomplete.** Read against run 892 (a 2-D subspace sufficient for the intervention and carrying almost none of the task) and run 890 (a planner that beats its baseline on a proxy and loses on the outcome), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps publishing small sufficient sets as if sufficiency were coverage.** Mechanical rule for us: **every nominated component set our white-box model produces is printed as a triple on the same prompt - probability or score under plain masking, under an optimised attack, and the share of incoming attribution it carries - and a set that wins the first column and loses the second is filed as sufficient-not-covering, with the attack number beside it rather than in an appendix.** Corollary the paper supplies: generalisation of the small set to a paraphrased prompt (0.895 here) is not evidence of coverage either, since the same attack kills it there too.
- **Pattern:** **Reproducibility across seeds and faithfulness can point opposite ways, and the paper prints the ordering against itself: cross-seed mean max cosine similarity is 0.4808 for its own read vectors and 0.5156 for write vectors (0.2826 for the rank-one products), against 0.8063 for a transcoder trained on local MSE and 0.4390/0.3468 for end-to-end transcoders - the method that loses on every faithfulness comparison in SS3.3 wins the consistency table by a wide margin.** Read against run 891 (a component's stability lowest exactly where it was most distinctive) and run 887 (a proxy trusted without its ceiling), the recurrence is that **the folder treats reproducibility as evidence for a decomposition without saying which property it is evidence of, and this entry is the first where the authors say out loud that a network may have a whole space of valid decompositions rather than one ground truth.** Mechanical rule for us: **a seed-consistency number never appears in our reports without the faithfulness number of the same object beside it, and if the two order methods differently the entry says which property we are claiming - agreement with our own reruns is a statement about our optimisation, not about the model.**

- **Pattern:** **A control arm built by deleting the hidden factor's influence changes the interpretation of every other arm, and here it moved the blame from the model to the estimator: rerunning the identical pipeline with the assignment coefficients set to zero leaves the marginal difficulty distribution intact, and under that regime the residual-corrected rollout estimator is still worse than plain imagination (curve MAE 0.066 versus 0.022 for CaLA) and still degrades the arm that sees the true latent (0.068 versus 0.016), so the failure cannot be latent inference and is filed against the continuous-treatment correction itself.** Read against run 892 (a certificate that passed while the mechanism was absent) and run 888 (a consistency score above every null while the steered response was worse than nothing), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps locating a cause by elimination on arms it chose, and this entry is the first where the elimination arm is a mechanism switch inside the data-generating process rather than a different model.** Mechanical rule for us: **any pipeline of ours that stacks a predictive component with a correction or calibration step is rerun with the confounding mechanism switched off but the input marginals preserved, and a correction that degrades estimates in that arm is reported as an estimator failure, not a modelling failure** - the two demand different fixes, and only the switch-off run distinguishes them.

- **Pattern:** **A model that ranks candidates well can still be unable to act, and this paper prints the two numbers from the same checkpoints: rank correlation with true cost rises from 0.49 to 0.80 and selection regret falls from 7.56 to 2.77 cost units while the chosen plans are systematically optimistic - predicted progress 10.9 px against realised 1.2 px - and the same 15 runs show no demonstrable coverage advantage over behaviour cloning (0.1 to 2.7 points, every interval spanning zero), with Diffusion Policy 16.7 points ahead on success.** Read against run 888 (consistency above every null at a horizon where the steered response was worse than doing nothing) and run 889 (interventional skill negative once the blind copy was subtracted), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps publishing a proxy that moves in the right direction while the target quantity does not, and this entry is the first where the proxy and the target are measured on identical frozen checkpoints with a stated do-nothing reference.** Mechanical rule for us: **any ranking, discrimination or consistency score our model reports is paired in the same row with the downstream quantity it is supposed to serve and with the best do-nothing baseline - and where the downstream comparison is with an imitation policy, that policy is the row, not a footnote**, because planning that is 0.3 points behind cloning on coverage but 9.5 ahead on success is a different claim from planning that simply loses.
- **Pattern:** **The useful intervention is identified by crossing two factors, not by swapping the whole system, and here the whole-system swap overstates it: replacing the entire learned model with the simulator reaches 89.9% restart coverage, exact scoring with learned proposals adds 12.2 points in every run, and exact proposals under learned scoring add nothing detectable - so the pipeline sits roughly 11 points short of a substitution it could make for free.** Read against run 886 (a multimodal graph whose machine half was exact and whose human half carried all the judgment) and run 885 (single-component effects not composing across interaction order), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps attributing a pipeline's behaviour to a named stage without ever holding the other stages fixed, and this entry is the cheapest printed remedy on disk because one of the two factors is the ground-truth simulator itself.** Mechanical rule for us: **when our white-box model nominates a component as the cause of a downstream failure, the evidence is a crossed substitution - each stage independently swapped for the reference implementation, the other stages frozen - and the headline is the single-arm contrast, never the all-stages contrast; a stage that shows no detected gain is reported as such rather than dropped from the factorial**, since the null arm is what establishes that the other arm is not an artefact of the combined swap.
- **Pattern:** **Exposure on the training manifold certifies nothing about the queries the decision rule will make, and the cleanest evidence here is that the two models are indistinguishable where experts acted and diverge sharply where they did not: under recorded actions the state error is 0.011 against 0.012, while under random actions the demonstration-only model scores 0.025 against a 0.023 zero-action reference - it is worse than predicting nothing - and the counterfactually trained model scores 0.007.** Read against run 889 (a blind copy whose held-out skill was real but whose interventional skill was negative) and run 887 (portability measured only into a competent target), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps validating predictors on the same distribution that produced their training targets, and this entry is the first where the off-support arm has a stated reference error so "worse than a constant" is a legible result rather than a small number.** Mechanical rule for us: **every prediction test on our white-box model has an on-support arm and an off-support arm, the off-support arm carries the error of the best constant baseline on the same inputs, and a model whose off-support error exceeds that constant is reported as not yet carrying the dynamics, whatever its on-support number says.** Two corollaries worth copying: the ablation that blocks prediction gradients into the shared encoder leaves reactive behaviour inconclusive (5.1 points, interval spanning zero) but costs 44.3 points of restart coverage, so the encoder's value is visible only under the search query; and the supplied-state ablation costs 31.5 points, so a shared representation is a diagnostic convenience rather than an advantage - a separately trained state-space model shows no coverage difference and 12.0 points more success.

- **Pattern:** **A held-out score can be entirely explained by what the input says about the population rather than the treatment, and this paper is the first in the folder where the control is a copy of the same model with the causal variable amputated: the registry model removes 21% of baseline error on risk differences (0.211 [0.141, 0.281] against the global mean) yet scores -0.12 [-0.21, -0.05] against its own blind copy, i.e. giving it the drug made it worse than not knowing, and the blind copy alone scores 0.297.** Read against run 883 (a contrastive representation whose 0.94 linear separation was the loss rather than a measurement) and run 888 (a consistency score beating every null while its steered response was worse than doing nothing), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps finding that an accuracy number and the competence it is supposed to certify come apart, and this entry supplies the cheapest instrument yet for separating them - one refit, no labels beyond the ones already there.** Mechanical rule for us: **every predictor our white-box model publishes for behaviour under intervention is accompanied by a blind-copy score computed from an identical model with the intervention-identifying inputs removed and nothing else changed, and the two numbers are reported as a pair (skill against the raw baseline, skill against the blind copy); a system that passes only the first is described as predicting the setting, never the mechanism.** The negative sign is the honest form of the degenerate case and should be reported as it prints, not floored at zero.

- **Pattern:** **A benchmark repair can be worth more than a model improvement, and here it moved the headline by 0.12: fixing arm pairing - same-molecule exclusion, concurrency, investigational-arm preference - dropped 1,510 of 11,274 contrasts and cut the language model's posted-record interventional skill from 0.39 to 0.27, because the discarded cases were exactly the ones where the "intervention" field was a restatement of the outcome.** Read against run 885 (an annotation-based selection rule that quietly truncated the graph) and run 886 (a legible subset masking an unrepresentative one), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps finding that the data-construction step, not the method, decides the number, and this entry is the first where the construction is audited twice and the audit is printed with the delta it caused.** Mechanical rule for us: **any pairing, matching or alignment step in our evaluation (which read-out goes with which intervention, which edited network is compared with which original) is audited on a random sample of at least 100 units with the valid fraction stated, and the headline is recomputed on the repaired set with both versions printed side by side** - because a re-pairing that lifts validity from 76% to 96% can also move the result by more than the thing being measured, and only the pair shows it. Second mechanical consequence, the author's own discipline: report the sensitivity case (here v2) as a row rather than deleting it, so a reader can see the size of the correction.

- **Pattern:** **The folder's own reading site, the relative depth 0.8 the last three entries have debated, is worth less than the coordinate system the read is written in: two models matched on native width and depth (Llama-3.1-8B and Mistral-7B, both 32 layers and 4096 wide, both read at the same relative depth) transfer native probes at chance - 42.5 to 69.5 on trivia output prediction, 19.6 to 59.0 on GT - while the identical probe on 300 anchor-identity coordinates transfers at 98.3 to 99.9 on the same pairs and the same data.** Read against run 884 (a selector that picks where to read) and run 882 (a layer score searching for a stable site), the recurrence is that **the folder has spent several entries optimising a read site inside one model's basis, and this entry is the first where the basis itself is changed and the site question dissolves** - the global construction aggregates every layer precisely so that corresponding layers never have to be chosen. Mechanical rule for us: **whenever our white-box model compares two networks, the comparison object is defined relative to a declared reference set (inputs, anchors, directions on a held-out basis) rather than to either network's native coordinates, and the report prints the same-width native-transfer baseline beside it, because matching dimensions is not matching bases and only the matched pair exposes the difference.** Corollary the paper's own ablation supplies: global aggregation is not a small win over a well-chosen local layer - it removes a hyperparameter and is reported as a depth-free default rather than a superior one, local probes at validation-selected depths never beating it consistently.
- **Pattern:** **Portability of an explanation and decodability of its target are two different facts, and the paper prints the cleanest separation on disk: on MATH, calibrated transfer into GPT-OSS-20B sits at 52.4 - essentially chance - while a probe trained on GPT-OSS itself reaches 78.5, so the property is linearly present in the target and the source's decision boundary simply does not apply to it.** Read against run 881 (a proxy near-exact on one architecture and dead on another under identical data) and run 879 (explanation surviving a change of intervention unit and not a change of trained solution), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps publishing a single AUROC as evidence that a concept lives in a model, when that number is the product of two quantities - whether the property is there and whether the reader's boundary is the right one - and the failure modes look identical when only one is printed.** Mechanical rule for us: **no cross-model or cross-checkpoint transfer number enters our model's report without a target-fitted reference probe in the same row; a transfer score at chance with a target-fitted score at 78.5 is filed as \"the target computes it differently\", never as \"the target does not compute it\".** Second consequence, from the same paper's 36-cell correlation (target answer accuracy versus mean incoming transfer, Spearman 0.976, Pearson 0.888): **transfer quality is a function of the target's competence**, so a monitor validated on a strong model carries no guarantee for a weak one - which the 1B/8B/70B ladder shows in both directions (1B to 70B 94.8 against 96.0 same-model; 70B to 1B 50.5 against 68.2).
- **Pattern:** **A proxy for a model's internal quantity can be trusted only when the paper also prints what its ceiling is and what happens when the reference set is degraded, and here both: transfer keeps 85.0% of same-model AUROC above chance on guard because the ceiling is 44.9 points, 90.7% on trivia GT because 39.1, and blind recovery of anchor identity reaches only 20.7% - yet probes applied through that mostly-wrong mapping retain more than 90% of their AUROC.** Read against run 883 (a variance share at 0.23 that carried the class separation) and run 880 (a share-of-layer at 82% beside a share-of-source at 36%), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps quoting a ratio whose denominator it does not print, and this entry is the first where the denominator is a stated ceiling and the numerator's sensitivity to reference-set error is measured rather than asserted.** Mechanical rule for us: **every retention-style ratio our model reports is printed as (value, ceiling, retention of excess over chance) in one triple, and every construction that relies on a reference set carries an ablations row in which that set is deliberately corrupted - anchors averaged over different completions (at most 2.7 points of change), anchors with 79% of identities wrong (more than 90% retained) - so the reader can see whether the model's dependence is on the set's semantics or on exact correspondence.** Corollary worth keeping: the paper attributes transfer to the semantic organisation of the anchor set rather than to one-to-one identity, which is what makes the method robust to two models tokenising the same anchor differently.

- **Pattern:** **A representation trained to separate two classes will separate them, and the separation accuracy is then the loss rather than a measurement - this paper's over-0.94 linear accuracy is produced by a contrastive objective that names the cross-scheme pairs as negatives, is already high at the first convolutional layer, and is reported with no probe on raw fields and no randomly initialised encoder as a control.** Read against run 882 (a layer chosen by an explicit stability score and reported with its runner-up) and run 879 (an attribution score whose identification half sat at AUROC 0.91+ even in mismatched rows), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps quoting a number whose upper bound was set by the training objective, and this entry is the cleanest case because the objective is self-supervised and per-class by construction, so the probe can only confirm what gradient descent was asked to do.** Mechanical rule for us: **any separation, decodability or classification accuracy our white-box model reports carries a matched control arm - the same probe on the raw read-out, and the same probe on a randomly initialised encoder of the same shape - and a result that survives neither is filed as task-success rather than as evidence about content.** Corollary the paper's own layer curve supplies: because the first layer already discriminates, a reader given only the ceiling number would attribute the separation to depth it does not need.
- **Pattern:** **A direction can hold almost none of a representation's variance and all of its discriminative content, and the paper prints the pair in one sentence: the final-layer embedding is essentially two-dimensional, yet the third component - 0.23 percent of the variance - is where the two microphysics schemes separate cleanly while the first two hold the seasonal cycle and mix them.** Read against run 880 (a head carrying 82% of its layer's reader effect but 36% of the source movement) and run 878 (a representation holding 71.8% of the gradient energy and 34.7% of the causal gap), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps using explained variance, energy share or aggregate sensitivity as a proxy for relevance, and every one of those entries ends with the proxy and the target disagreeing.** Mechanical rule for us: **no direction or component in our model is ranked, kept or discarded on its share of activation variance; the only filter is its score against the intervention it is supposed to predict, and when a variance share is reported it is reported beside that score so the two can be seen diverging.** Second mechanical consequence: **the compression layer matters** - the same paper's three dense layers fall from the second to the final in classification skill while the final layer improves the similarity structure the loss actually targets, so a projection head is a redesign of the space and any probe placed after it is probing the objective, not the model.
- **Pattern:** **A two-way comparison needs a third anchor before its numbers mean anything about error, and this paper's ordering is the schema: the two model configurations are closer to each other than either is to observations, and the configuration with the more detailed physics is the closer of the two, with the looser one also carrying visibly larger ensemble spread against the reference.** Read against run 876 (three references making the same policy look twice as good or twice as bad) and run 877 (a comparison against the method's own template rather than against the field), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps publishing a distance between two objects as though distance were quality, and this entry is the first where both pairwise distances to a shared external reference are printed so "they differ" and "they are wrong" are separable by construction.** Mechanical rule for us: **every comparison our white-box model makes between an edited network and its original is printed as a triangle - edited versus original, edited versus a held-out reference behaviour, original versus that same reference - and the claim is made only on the side of the triangle that carries it; a large edited-versus-original distance with both sides equidistant from the reference is a statement about the edit, never about degradation.** Related warning this paper supplies for free: its parameter-correlation stage scans a large grid of region-variable-parameter triples at 100 members against a bare Pearson 0.3 bar with no multiplicity correction and reports the same region with opposite signs across comparisons without resolving them, which is exactly the kind of table our model should publish with the scan size attached.

- **Pattern:** **A flip is a property of the distance to the boundary, not of the intervention's size, and this paper prints the two margins that make the point in one table: the identical source edit moves a next-token margin by 0.419754 nat and flips 17 to 15, while on a held-out wording a 0.360317-nat movement consumes 3.3% of a margin of 10.930855 and changes nothing; inside the switching prompt itself the same rule reappears in a dose scan, where all-L33 rescue ends at +0.014328 nat and gives 17 but at the higher dose ends at -0.004700 nat and gives 15.** Read against run 879 (identification and effect size printed as separate columns) and run 874 (block recovery at 1.000 beside coordinate matching near 0.68), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps scoring interventions in absolute units while the behaviour is thresholded, and this entry is the first where both the numerator and the denominator are printed in the same table so the flip rate cannot be read as a strength.** Mechanical rule for us: **every flip or downstream-change claim our white-box model makes carries the starting margin, the intervention's signed movement, and the fraction of that margin the movement consumes, on the same line; a count of flips without the starting-margin distribution is reported as an existence example and nothing more.** Corollary from the selection step: **if the exemplar was chosen because it flipped, the flip's frequency is unmeasured by construction**, which the authors state outright (one of 199 measured conditions, baseline margin 0.390 against a panel median of 19.775).
- **Pattern:** **The same immediate write produces final effects differing by a factor of 4.52, and the difference is created downstream rather than by the write: L33 head 26 and its complement emit perturbations of norm 1.739 and 1.733 with immediate readout contributions of +0.02237 and +0.02322 nat, yet their final margin movements are +0.15263 and +0.03374 nat, and jointly clamping L34-L35 MLP outputs collapses the gap from +0.118896 to +0.002480 nat.** Read against run 878 (a proxy holding 71.8% of gradient energy and 34.7% of the causal effect) and run 877 (a conditioning encoder never trained for the direction it was tested on), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps treating an intervention's immediate logit effect as its effect, and this entry supplies the cheapest possible test of that assumption - hold the next two modules' outputs fixed and see whether the comparison survives.** Mechanical rule for us: **any component-effect comparison our model publishes is run twice, once normally and once with the two modules downstream of the compared components clamped at their no-intervention values, and the pair of numbers is printed; a component whose relative effect depends on that clamp is described as conditionally contributing rather than as strongly contributing.** Second mechanical consequence: **a clamp can strengthen one component and weaken the other, so the clamp is a transformation of the comparison rather than a correction to it** - holding L34 raised the complement's effect to +0.062106 while holding L35 lowered it to +0.010002, and in the reused context holding L34 increased the complement's effect by +0.010646 nat with L35 free but decreased it by 0.011835 nat with L35 held, so background conditions belong on every effect row.
- **Pattern:** **One denominator makes an explanation look localized and another exposes how little it covers, and the paper puts both on one figure axis: head 26 carries about 82% of the all-L33 reader effect but only 36% of the source movement, the L32-33 cache window carries about 68% of the margin difference in each direction while values alone carry about 54% and keys about 14%, and replacing the complement instead of the nominated head also crosses the boundary and restores 17.** Read against run 871 (a single sufficient neuron published beside its second and third) and run 869 (a distributed signal whose per-layer contribution was about 0.01 against a cumulative gap near 50), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps reporting a component's share of its own layer as though it were its share of the behaviour, and this entry is the first where both shares are labelled separately and the ratio between them is printed.** Mechanical rule for us: **every component our model nominates is reported as share-of-layer and share-of-source-effect as two columns that are never multiplied into a path probability, and any behavioural pivot it produces is published beside the complement's pivot, because a pivot that the complement also produces identifies a boundary crosser rather than the largest contributor.**

- **Pattern:** **This is the folder's first entry where the cost of an explanation is the object of a formal error budget, and the budget has a term no amount of data can reduce - which is the single most useful template the head has found for reporting a conditional predictor.** Theorem 3 splits the atlas error into irreducible representation error, local target-instability error and finite-source error, and the paper says outright that only the last shrinks with more sources, so the ranking of what to fix is fixed before any experiment runs. Read against run 877 (an amortised hypernetwork whose conditioning encoder was never trained for the direction it was tested in) and run 870 (a scheduler that collapsed when handed more budget), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps finding that a conditional system fails on the axis its authors did not model as costly, and this entry is the first to publish that axis as a named term with a bound.** Mechanical rule for us: **every conditional prediction our white-box model publishes carries the same three-way split - representation error, local-instability error, finite-sample error - and states which term more data can reduce, because a reader who is told only the total error will spend effort on the wrong knob.** Second mechanical consequence from the same theorem: **the stochastic term is independent of the number of parameter groups because every profile lies on a simplex; normalised simplex-valued targets buy a sample-complexity guarantee that raw-magnitude scores do not, and our per-group scores should be normalised for the same reason.**
- **Pattern:** **A method can capture most of a quantity's proxy and a third of the quantity, and this paper prints both columns side by side in the same table - which makes it the folder's cleanest instance of a first-order score failing to transfer to a causal effect.** At 0.1% on vision, semantic KPSA holds 71.8% of the direct-gradient energy yet recovers 34.7% of the causal gap, with the same dilution at every setting (72.9/46.5 on ETTh1, 74.6/50.2 on Weather, 42.8/33.2 on protein); the paper's own reading is that the infinitesimal target and the finite perturbation are bridged only by a smooth local argument, not identified. - **Pattern:** **The conditioning representation, not the estimator, decides whether the method works, and the paper's own ablation set shows a categorical space winning one modality outright and scoring a zero-crossing interval in another.** The categorical query space beats the learned representation in vision (39.4% gap against 34.7%, 75.8% energy) while collapsing to 2.2% on ETTh1 with an interval that crosses zero, 5.6% on Weather and 5.4% on protein; the 1NN ablation beats the kernel average on ETTh1 (52.4% against 46.5%) and loses on Weather (46.7% against 50.2%); and in neuron localisation categorical KPSA beats semantic on vision (76.5% against 66.5%) while scoring 4.4% on protein against 68.3%.
