- **Pattern:** **A coherence axiom can be provably satisfied, auditable to machine precision, and worth nothing for accuracy, and the paper prints the head-to-head that says so: the exact coarsening-consistent operator has a KL gap near 10^-17 while the per-level lookup baseline it replaces sits at 0.02-0.05, yet a deliberately inconsistent marginaliser with identical information access beats the shared table by 0.048 and 0.034 nats at k = 0 and k = 1 on IEMOCAP and by 0.041 and 0.015 on M3ED, and the cost of sharing shrinks as data shrinks (0.029 to 0.021 overall on IEMOCAP) with the sparsest cells flipping in the shared table's favour.** Read against run 874 (block recovery at 1.000 beside coordinate matching at 0.68, ranking reversing between datasets) and run 870 (a policy with a real predictive surface and no lift over hold), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps producing invariant-respecting objects and then having to admit the invariant is not the thing being measured, and this entry is the cleanest case because the invariance is cheap to audit exactly, the violation is a number the authors publish rather than a caveat, and the bias-variance account predicts in advance which side wins where.** Mechanical rule for us: **every structural guarantee our white-box model claims - consistency under coarsening, equivariance under a rotation, monotonicity under more evidence - is published beside a head-to-head against a deliberately anti-compliance baseline with identical information access, in the same table, with the density regime where each wins named; a gap near zero and a small NLL difference are two different claims and the paper shows they can point opposite ways.** Corollary, from the deployment framing: the value that survives is one table serving every level and every panel size at a quantified cost (0.0085 nats against the stronger baseline, halving to 0.0044 once that baseline loses its oracle training data), which is a service property and not an accuracy property.
- **Pattern:** **The reference a policy is scored against can make it look twice as good or twice as bad depending on whether the reference is achievable, and the paper reports three references for the same cells: the target-free water-filling policy recovers 83 and 93 percent of a retrospective feature-class headroom on IEMOCAP and M3ED at budget one, 35 and 41 percent of a clairvoyant oracle, and 23 and 26 percent of the retrospective bound for a simple entropy-binning policy in the same cells - and on EmoWOZ, where it loses to uniform by 0.021 nats, the retrospective bound beats uniform by only 0.007, which diagnoses the loss as features that carry no row-level signal rather than a broken policy.** Read against run 872 (a location/ordering/shape triplet that disagrees inside every model) and run 863 (a router margin at chance on the downstream quantity), the recurrence is that **the folder's negative results keep needing an explanation of whether the method failed or the target was noise, and this entry supplies the third reference that separates the two.** Mechanical rule for us: **every allocation, selection or steering policy our white-box model proposes is reported against hold or uniform, against a feature-class bound fit in-sample on the evaluation block (with the realisation caveat stated), and against the clairvoyant oracle - because the oracle price conflates estimation error with irreducible target randomness, and a policy that loses to uniform where the achievable bound is near zero nats is a correct policy on a target with nothing to gain.** Second mechanical consequence, from the same table: **a proxy metric is not a substitute for the direct measurement.** The cross-turn curve and the same-item curve have row-wise Spearman correlation 0.266 at k = 0 and 0.011 at k = 1 on IEMOCAP, so the paper runs the direct held-out-rater rotation instead of using its own curve as a proxy - - **Pattern:** **The same validated read-outs are inert for one head and causal for another head trained on the identical frozen representation, and the paper prints both verdicts in one table row: zeroing the bright-clean latent moves the direction head by 0.034 degrees against 0.024 for matched controls and clears no causal rule, while the same removal moves an uncertainty head's predicted log error by 0.31 and the whole 194-latent clean family by 0.78, in every one of four independently trained dictionaries.** Read against run 869 (a detection direction whose intervention was wrong-signed on the same axis) and run 868 (a behaviour found and attributed but not repaired), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps discovering that a feature's causal status is a property of a reader rather than of the feature, and this entry is the first where two readers on one frozen representation are compared under one fixed protocol and diverge that hard.** Mechanical rule for us: **every causal claim our white-box model publishes names the read-out it is causal for, and a feature whose effect is null for one reader is filed as unused by that reader, never as inert, because a dictionary that is causally dead for a head which does not need the concept is evidence about the head and only becomes evidence about the feature when a head that does need it is also tested.** Corollary the authors state in almost these terms: absence from one dictionary at one layer is not absence from the model, since the depth concept is invisible at the final layer (best raw AUROC 0.598, nothing retained) and sharp at layer 2 (0.986, control 0.984) without being a bottleneck for the head.
- **Pattern:** **A sensitivity axis can be stable, replicated, causal and still describe the population rather than the event, and the paper gives the two numbers that separate those claims: the leading axis agrees across independent splits to within 5.6 degrees, carries 98 percent of the aggregate sensitivity, and no verified latent exceeds an absolute cosine of 0.15 with it, yet the median event's own Jacobian puts essentially none of its local sensitivity on that axis while the sample mean puts 14.9 percent there.** Read against run 869 (a distributed signal whose per-layer contribution was about 0.01 against a cumulative gap near 50) and run 864 (a redundancy buffer under which any ranking rule looks validated), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps producing aggregate objects whose per-instance meaning was never checked, and this entry is the first to print the aggregate share beside the per-instance share in the same paragraph and to draw the opposite conclusion for the second head, whose axis carries 78 percent of the variance and a median of 77 percent of each event's sensitivity.** Mechanical rule for us: **every direction, axis or dictionary entry our model publishes with an aggregate statistic also carries the median per-instance share of that statistic, and a large aggregate share with a near-zero median is published as a population summary rather than as a mechanism - because a head with no common bottleneck and a head with one genuinely shared mechanism look identical under the aggregate and differ only by that median.** Second mechanical consequence, cheap and testable: **a matching dictionary trained to preserve the head's output should recover the head's sensitivity axis if the axis is real**, and here it does at an absolute cosine near 0.8, which is the kind of cross-object confirmation our model should be required to pass.
- **Pattern:** **A coordinate can be causally load-bearing and still not be a concept, and the paper's own dose response is what separates the two readings: the latent with the largest mean-activation contrast is dense, fails every selectivity control, discriminates high from low charge per event at chance (0.532 against a 0.516 control), yet zeroing it costs 15.0 degrees of angular error on bright events and 10.9 on dim ones, an intervention between 11.6 and 14.8 degrees across four dictionaries, with a V-shaped dose curve whose minimum sits at the coordinate's unperturbed value.** Read against run 871 (a single neuron whose removal and repair were the same intervention at two doses) and run 866 (a transcoder that improved reconstruction while worsening attribution), the recurrence is that **the folder's causal prominence and its semantic promiscuity keep coming apart, and this entry is the first where the artifact has a name - a support coordinate - and a diagnostic (the V-shape) that distinguishes supporting a well-formed representation from encoding a monotonic quantity.** Mechanical rule for us: **any coordinate our model finds either semantically validated or causally prominent but not both is published under a distinct label, and a non-monotone dose response is reported as support rather than as a feature, because a model can depend on a coordinate without reading it as any quantity, and the two mistakes available to a reader - discarding a support coordinate as noise, or promoting it to a concept - are both avoidable only if the dose shape is printed.** Also mechanical, from the same result: **a set-level null has to price its own contamination**, since the paper's negative seed shows a 194-latent family ablation costing about 10 degrees precisely because the family contained a support latent that does not validate as a concept.

masking, patching, prefix injection, a pinned coordinate - the reported curvature or confidence is accompanied by the variance of the latent explanation posterior on the same inputs and by the score gap between the leading explanations, because confidence under an intervention and confidence under the marginal model are two different matrices and the difference between them is exactly that rank-one correction.** Also mechanical: **the report names which parameter block was updated.** The paper's reassuring arm (noise scales only) and its damaging arm (noise plus drift) both raise held-out evidence, and only the arm that moved the drift changed the dynamical quantities, so "the update improved the objective" is uninformative until it says what block moved.

- **Pattern:** **The gate is narrower than any direction ever proposed for it, and the paper prints the basis contrast that makes this measurable: the identical gradient-times-activation ranking run on MLP post-activations lands on a single scalar that reaches 91.7% LLM-judge attack success on the held-out set (91.9% under Llama-Guard) and matches a whole-network direction ablation that touches every layer (93.1% and 91.6%), while the same ranking run on residual-stream coordinates tops out at 45% on Llama-3.1-8B and 39% on Qwen3-8B at its best constant - and the reason is printed as distribution overlap, since the best residual coordinates separate harmful from harmless almost not at all while the winning MLP neurons separate them cleanly.** Read against run 869 (six detection methods all at ceiling, every intervention weak, wrong-signed or null) and run 862 (seed variance across five vectors that all produced the behaviour), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps discovering that the unit a behaviour is written in is an assumption nobody tested, and this entry is the first to run one selector in two bases and let the attack success rate decide.** Mechanical rule for us: **every white-box candidate our model selects is selected twice - once in the site the method naturally assumes and once in the rotation-invariant alternative - and the two read-outs are published side by side with the distribution separation that explains the gap, because a selector that works only in a privileged basis is reporting a fact about the basis, and the folder's direction-level results are only as good as their assumption that the residual stream is where the quantity lives.** Also mechanical: **a single-unit claim carries its own counter-evidence.** These authors report that one model has a second and a third independently sufficient neuron, and publish them rather than compressing the story to one - our model must report the multiplicity of sufficient units it finds, because "one neuron suffices" and "only one neuron suffices" are different claims and rapid papers blur them.
- **Pattern:** **Two independent identification routes converging on one unit is the strongest evidence in this entry, and the disagreement rate is published rather than hidden: gradient-times-activation and pure weight geometry - cosine of the refusal direction against the down-projection rows, tested against an analytic random-directions null - land on the exact same neuron in two of seven models (Qwen3-1.7B at layer 13 and Llama-3.1-70B at layer 25), which the authors call evidence of structural encoding, while the other five models select different layers and are explained away by the cosine route being restricted to one layer.** Read against run 864 (a ranking statistic that cleared correction at exactly one layer of one model) and run 863 (an oracle and a random selector that both failed to beat hold), the recurrence is that **the folder's method-agreement checks are usually a single correlation to a reference vector, which run 862 already showed cannot identify the object, and this entry is the first to build a second identification route out of the weights alone and score the two against each other.** Mechanical rule for us: **when our model names a unit as the one responsible, the entry reports a second, method-independent route to the same unit plus a null distribution - and when the two routes pick different units, that is reported as a disagreement count rather than dropped, because 2-of-7 agreement ten octaves past a null is a real finding and 5-of-7 disagreement is the boundary condition on it.** Corollary from the null itself: the expected maximum cosine of random unit rows at these dimensions is 0.05 to 0.10, so **any cosine we publish as evidence is quoted against that expectation, never against zero**, because at these widths a cosine of 0.15 looks large and is only about two to three times the random maximum.
- **Pattern:** **The removal and the repair of a behaviour can be the same intervention at two doses with one context-sensitivity term between them, and the paper prices the middle option: pinning one scalar to a fixed value at every token position removes refusal at 91.9% attack success but costs 8.8 MMLU points on average and 18.2 on the largest model, and the anchor variant - the same neuron, the same direction, with the multiplier scaled by how strongly each prompt already fires that neuron and clamped - keeps 90.1% and costs 0.6 MMLU, which is a fifteenfold reduction in damage for one point of effect.** Read against run 870 (a scheduler that collapsed from 0.9125 to 0.49375 when given a bigger budget) and run 866 (a sparsity pairing rule where the training-time budget is set away from the target), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps publishing interventions at a single operating point and calling the side-effect intrinsic to the method, when the side-effect is a function of how unconditionally the intervention is applied.** Mechanical rule for us: **every intervention our model proposes is published as at least a two-point family - unconditional and conditionally scaled on a per-input read of the same unit - with effect and damage both printed at each point, because the paper's own two rows differ by an order of magnitude in capability cost at near-identical attack success and a reader given only the first row would conclude the site is expensive when it is the pinning that is.** Second mechanical consequence, from the same table: **a capability cost must be reported per model, not just averaged**, because the same recipe costs 0.6 MMLU on the smallest Qwen and 18.2 on the 70B Llama, and an average of 8.8 describes neither.

- **Pattern:** **The paper prints a predictive surface with real headroom beside a policy over that surface with none, and the two numbers sit in the same subsection: the retrospective best action is worth 0.668542, a state-gated policy built from the measured response map lifts composite utility by only +0.014683 over doing nothing, selects the best action in 33.333% of 504 complete matrices, and in the stochastic panel there are 253 opportunity-positive blocks out of 1,248 with 0/104 held-out opportunity captures and 0/516 selected nonidentity admissions, while the same paper's observers predict the outcome family at 93.57% and 91.74%.** Read against run 869 (perfect detection, failed control, six methods) and run 863 (a router margin that detected route flips at AUC 0.772 and sat at chance on harm), the recurrence is that **the folder now has three entries in five runs where the measurement succeeds and the policy over the measurement does not, and this one is the first to print the oracle gap and the capture rate as the two numbers that make the failure legible.** Mechanical rule for us: **every policy our white-box model claims is reported as four numbers on one line - realized lift over hold, retrospective oracle utility, gap between them, and the fraction of cells where the policy picked the oracle action - because a predictive surface with headroom and a policy with no lift are the same model scored two ways, and only the gap and the selection rate tell a reader which one they are looking at.** Also mechanical: **hold is a positive action.** The paper's saturated cells require no added effort and its state-estimator decomposition shows that correct baseline-state estimation is what carries the effect (+0.626 with 95% lower bound +0.196, against +0.056 with lower bound -0.101 for wrong or unresolved estimates), so our model's default must be an explicit no-intervention prediction that the evaluator scores, not a skipped row.
- **Pattern:** **Added effort is not monotone and the sign of a drive is a function of its dose, its bath and the state of the receiver: the same scheduler that reached composite utility 0.9125 collapsed to 0.49375 with damage 0.1125 when given a larger budget and to 0.31875 with damage 0.1500 with an always-on stronger field, a dose sweep took format invalidity from +0.120 to +0.266 while target fell from +0.078 to +0.031, and the local-admittance tensor found 706 sign-changing cells over 56,212 rows beside 2,587 stiff or saturated ones - i.e. roughly one cell in eighteen where more of the same drive reverses its effect.** Read against run 860 (a fine-tune that concentrated route weights where the folder already expected them) and run 859 (a residual-state arm that beat the direction arm at the same site), the recurrence is that **the folder's intervention entries keep assuming a monotone dose-response and this is the first to measure the non-monotone region rather than infer it.** Mechanical rule for us: **any steering or ablation our model predicts carries at least two doses and the sink channels at each - target gain beside damage, null, invalid-format and effort - and a drive whose sink cost rises faster than its target gain is published as overdrive rather than as a stronger version of the working case, because "the intervention works" and "the intervention works at this dose" are different claims and the paper's own numbers move one point of dose from a gain into a loss.**
- **Pattern:** **An adapter, a constitution and a prompt are media and drives rather than controls, and the null baseline is not inert: the standard editorial-principle adapter beats the null-random adapter by +0.453125 on matched cells and the editorial/NIST comparator surface by +0.140625, yet the authors insist the null-random adapter is itself an active trained medium with its own susceptibility surface rather than noise - so the control arm of the folder's most common comparison is a second treatment.** Read against run 865 (a control that shared the treatment's provenance) and run 861 (a matched non-target null that turned a read-out into a statement about a probe), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps finding that its baselines are treatments, and this entry is the first to name the consequence for adapter and constitution studies explicitly.** Mechanical rule for us: **every "random" or "null" control our white-box model reports is validated as inert before it is used as a comparator - the same probe battery and the same utility readout run on the null as on the treatment - and a null that moves the readout at all is published as a second condition, because a comparison against a live medium measures the difference between two media, not the effect of one.**

No figure inspected as an image - the pipeline diagram and the geometry plots are described only through captions and prose.
- **Pattern:** **The direction that reads a behaviour and the direction that writes it are nearly orthogonal whenever the behaviour is a substrate rather than an overlay, and the paper prices that with one number: hallucination detection is perfect by six independent methods (linear probe AUC 1.000 from layer 5, single head AUC 1.000, logit-lens 0.913, neuron 88%, SAE 88%/0%, embedding norm 83%) while the detection direction sits at cosine 0.12 from the refusal direction on a 0.02 chance floor, and every intervention built from it is weak, wrong-signed or null, whereas format collapses both roles onto a single vector.** Read against run 868 (a forecast scored on held-out interventions) and run 863 (a router margin that detected route flips at AUC 0.772 and sat at chance on harm given a flip), the recurrence is that **the folder now has five consecutive entries where a read-out's quality does not license an interventional claim, and this one is the cheapest decomposition of why: the read-out is a class of directions while the control is one direction, and the two classes are not related by a rotation you can read off statically.** Mechanical rule for us: **every read-out our white-box model publishes is paired with the intervention direction built from the same unit set, their cosine is printed against the dimension-scaled chance floor, and a read-out whose control direction does not itself detect the behaviour is published as a detector on a different axis - because "the model knows" and "the model acts on what it knows" are two subspaces, and the paper's own Llama case proves the second can be right while the first is geometrically unrelated to it.**
- **Pattern:** **A large effect along a probe direction does not mean the output mapping reads it: the fake-vs-real gap on that axis is +49.8 (6.9x a random-direction mean), yet the refusal gap on the same axis is -24.9 in the wrong direction, removing the projection entirely leaves the model's prediction of "Nor" on "Norlandia" essentially unchanged, and the residual component orthogonal to it - dominated by entity copy - outweighs it by a median ~12x, and outweighs it MORE on real entities, so the domination is a property of the output mapping and not of the failure case.** Read against run 867 (an SAE whose features labelled letter fragments while the ordering property appeared in none of them) and run 866 (a transcoder that improved KL while worsening the attribution score), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps finding signals that are strong, real and inert, and this entry is the first to give the reason as a magnitude comparison inside one vector space rather than as a caveat.** Mechanical rule for us: **any signal our model reports carries its orthogonal complement as a competing number - the gap along the candidate direction beside the norm of the residual orthogonal to it - and a candidate whose orthogonal component dominates is published as descriptive of the state, never as causal to the output, because a probe can be near-perfect and still live in a slice the output mapping ignores, and the ratio is what tells you which.**
- **Pattern:** **A signal distributed across layers can be real and unusable as a gate: each late MLP layer contributes only about 0.01 to the detection projection while the cumulative gap reaches ~50, so all 9 self-intervention gate conditions came out at baseline, even though the same signal drives a 6.9x-above-random gap once summed - and attention from layer 17 on is not merely redundant but mildly opposed, since deleting it raises fake-entity refusal from 60% to 65% at 100% of real answers intact.** Read against run 864 (a redundancy buffer under which any ranking rule looks validated) and run 859 (a residual-state arm that beat the direction arm at the same site), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps proposing per-unit or per-layer triggers and keeps discovering the quantity it wants lives at a different granularity.** Mechanical rule for us: **a per-layer or per-feature trigger our model proposes reports the per-unit contribution and the cumulative signal separately, and a trigger whose unit-level value is below what its own baseline noise requires is reported as needing a multi-layer read-out - because "the model represents it" and "any one layer represents enough of it to act on" differ by the accumulation, and the paper's 0.01-against-50 is the cleanest instance of that gap on disk.**

- **Pattern:** **An intervention that moves along the shortest path between two points in activation space is not a small change to the concept, it is a change to whether the model is in a state it has ever occupied - and the post prices that difference the cheap way: it trains an action model on a simulated physics world, fits a curve to the encoder's position representations, and shows the predicted car sliding smoothly when the edit follows the curve while a straight path between the same endpoints produces incoherent output or lands the car somewhere else entirely.** Read against run 866 (transcoding that turned a helix into lookup tables and scored better on KL while scoring worse as an attribution) and run 865 (a decodability probe that cleared on a subspace while the ablated direction did nothing), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps finding interventions whose validity depends on staying on the data manifold while the methods that report success are all off-manifold aggregates.** Mechanical rule for us: **every intervention our white-box model proposes is run twice - along a fitted path through the occupied set and along the straight difference between the endpoints - and the two outcomes are reported together with a check that the intermediates are near the data; a method that only works on the straight path and a method that only works on the curve are describing different objects, and here the straight path fails in the specific way that matters (silently arriving at a different valid state), which no scalar error would have caught.**
- **Pattern:** **A dictionary can be complete over a structure and still not name the structure: the SAE features that reconstruct the rhyme manifold carry labels about leading letter fragments and morphology (words beginning with a syllable, a token showing up in titles), while the property that orders the manifold - the ending sound - appears in none of them, and the authors' word for this is shattering.** Read against run 864 (a router margin that detected flips and knew nothing about harm) and run 861 (a probe that survived only on its own fitting distribution), the recurrence is that **the folder's feature-level entries keep separating what a feature fires on from what the region it belongs to means, and this is the first entry where the separation is visible in the labels themselves rather than inferred from a metric.** Mechanical rule for us: **when our model publishes a feature, the entry prints both the feature's own firing description and the description of the smallest region the feature belongs to, and a feature whose own label carries less of the semantic load than its region's is reported as a tile of a larger structure rather than as a concept - because a dictionary that names every tile and no structure is complete at the wrong resolution, and the test for it is whether any single atom names the invariant, not whether the reconstruction is good.**

- **Pattern:** **Detecting an event and knowing whether the event is worth acting on are two different measurements, and here the first is easy and the second is at chance on the same signal: the deployable router margin scores route-flip occurrence at AUC 0.772, harm given a flip at 0.490 with P(harmful | flip) = 0.572, and benefit-vs-all at 0.499 - and when the oracle and a rate-matched random selector are both *executed* as selective-repair policies, the oracle buys nothing over random on OLMoE (+0.4%, CI includes 0) and only +2.3% on DeepSeek while the deployable gate sits *below* random on both.** Read against run 2607.27617 (a pre-registered 8.3% false-assertion rate against a 5% tolerance) and run 2604.03867 (a per-input router that captured a sliver of a 55-86% oracle), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps proposing selective or per-unit interventions and scoring them on the detection half of the problem, and this entry is the first to price the two halves separately and then score the policy end-to-end rather than summing its labels.** Mechanical rule for us: **every repair or selective-intervention trigger our white-box model proposes is scored on three populations with three numbers printed side by side - event occurrence, event harm given occurrence, and realized benefit of executing the policy against a rate-matched random selector and an oracle - and a trigger that detects the event but sits at chance on harm is published as a detector, never as a control, because a gate that fires on 57% harmful events is a coin flip wearing a measuring instrument.**
- **Pattern:** **The signed decomposition near-cancels and the paper prints the components anyway: harmful route flips cost +0.043 nats and beneficial flips refund −0.047, the net two-sided tax is +0.0043 nats out of sample, and 90.2% cancellation replicates on a second architecture - which is why a direction-agnostic boundary-smoothing remedy nets roughly zero while a direction-aware clean-route pin recovers a bounded slice, and why the headline "routing carries about a third of the damage" is itself a ratio of signed quantities that a mean-ablation entry would report as a single number.** Read against run 2606.27091 (a sign flip in an ablation that turned a driver into a suppressor) and run 2605.01699 (a probe whose orientation decided the verdict), the recurrence is that **the folder's ablation and attribution entries keep reporting net effects whose constituent signs disagree, and this entry is the first to make the cancellation structure the result.** Mechanical rule for us: **every attribution, ablation or routing claim our white-box model publishes is reported as a signed component pair (harmful contribution, beneficial contribution, cancellation fraction) beside the net, and any remedy is classed as direction-agnostic or direction-aware before it is credited - because a symmetric intervention on a sign-balanced effect is guaranteed to return zero, and "the intervention fails" and "the intervention cancelled itself" are the same number and different findings.**
- **Pattern:** **A measured interaction kills the budget the naive decomposition would have produced: the quantized-context route path (+0.0175) is nearly twice the clean-context route path (+0.0092) and their difference is positive with a CI excluding zero, so compute damage and route damage are not additively separable at this dose and a route-only remedy cannot be costed as if the compute channel were held fixed - while the INT8 control's interaction collapses to −0.00006, showing the interaction scales with damage rather than being a property of the architecture.** Read against run 2607.27617 (a compression column and a fidelity column that disagreed by an order of magnitude) and run 2604.03867, the recurrence is that **the folder's decompositions keep being reported as additive shares and the share only means something when the interaction is measured.** Mechanical rule for us: **any channel decomposition our model publishes carries the interaction term as its own reported number with an interval, and when that interval excludes zero the entry states which direction it pushes the shares - because a two-path decomposition with an unmeasured interaction is a budget built on an assumption, and the interaction here is large enough to nearly double the routing share between the two contexts.**

- **Pattern:** **A fine-tune that looks like it learned a rule turns out to be a single added direction, and the paper proves it in the cheapest possible way - read the adapter's own output delta on twenty tokens of training data and twenty of an unrelated historical passage, take all 780 pairwise absolute cosines, and they sit near one for every task except the backdoor.** Read against run 2606.27091 (a fine-tune that concentrated an inherited route into fewer heads) and run 855 (a probe whose representation stopped tracking anything while accuracy held), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps trying to attribute a behavioural change to a structure, and the decisive instrument is almost always a difference between two models rather than anything inside one - here the difference is read at the module output and needs no training run of its own.** Mechanical rule for us: **every claim our white-box model makes about what a fine-tune, a distillation or a router changed is accompanied by the adapter-delta cosine diagnostic on matched in-distribution and out-of-distribution token blocks, and when the cosines are near one the claim is published as a direction plus a layer, because a change that is a direction has a sufficiency test (apply it alone) and a change that is not has no cheap test at all.**
- **Pattern:** **An unconditional vector produces a conditional behaviour: the Risky Backdoor vector is added at the final token of every prompt and the behaviour still appears only under a jailbreak string, with about 1.0 validation accuracy on unseen in-distribution backdoor examples while the OOD test accuracy is poor and below base - and patching the last-token query vectors from the base model into the steered model over a suffix of layers kills the jailbreak, which is where the condition turns out to live.** Read against run 852 (a causal certificate whose interchange accuracy did not predict usefulness) and run 2605.01699 (a matched non-target null that turned a read-out into a statement about a probe), the recurrence is that **the folder's behavioural conditionality keeps being attributed to the intervention when it belongs to the input, and the only entry that separated the two did it by making the injection position-invariant on purpose.** Mechanical rule for us: **a direction or probe our model describes as conditional is only published as conditional when the condition is localized to the input path - a patch or ablation that removes the trigger's influence while the direction stays applied - and a direction that looks conditional in behaviour but whose injection is position-invariant is reported as a constant edit interacting with a pre-existing gate, because the difference decides whether the deployed model's behaviour can be predicted from the direction alone.**
- **Pattern:** **The learned direction is not the obvious direction and not even the same direction twice: cosine to the naive mean-difference construction is low, and five seeds trained on the same function give vectors with low mutual cosine, yet every one of them produces the behaviour - so the object recovered is an equivalence class, and the cosine metric cannot identify it.** Read against run 2602.06801 (an affine-subspace proof that behaviour-compatible directions are a family) and run 2604.03867 (an oracle ceiling that made a small capture rate legible), the recurrence is that **the folder now has the same non-identifiability result twice from opposite directions - one proved analytically, one measured as seed variance in a real fine-tune - and no entry has yet published a behavioural equivalence test to go with it.** Mechanical rule for us: **when our model reports that it recovered the direction responsible for a behaviour, the evidence is a behavioural equivalence band (the recovered vectors, and norm-matched perturbations of them, all reproduce the effect within a stated tolerance) and never a cosine to a reference vector; and a seed-spread table is reported beside the headline so a reader sees how much of the geometry is arbitrary.**

- **Pattern:** **The distribution is the precondition, not the covariate, and the paper prices it twice from opposite directions: MMLU damage from the same recipe runs from minus 30.7 at one fitting pair to a flat plus 2.1 to 3.7 from thirteen pairs on for Llama 8B, while on Llama 70B it never leaves the negative range (minus 60.0 at one pair, minus 9.0 at three, plateau around minus 7.4 to minus 8.4), and when the same vectors are applied to a freshly generated question set the effect disappears entirely - no right skew at any strength between minus two and plus two.** Read against run 2604.03867 (per-prompt layer routing tuned and scored on the same datasets) and run 2611.07876 (a stimulus-only floor that reproduced the headline probe), the recurrence is that **the folder's steering results are all measured inside the distribution they were fitted on, and this entry is the first to build the shift and find nothing - which retroactively qualifies every steering number already on disk.** Mechanical rule for us: **every steering, removal or routing claim our white-box model publishes carries a declared fitting distribution and a matched-but-disjoint evaluation distribution, and the two numbers are reported side by side; a method whose effect survives only on its own fitting distribution is published as a fitting diagnostic, not as a control handle, because "the vector moves the behaviour" and "the vector moves the behaviour on text drawn the same way" are one sentence apart and one of them is what deployment needs.** A second, sharper corollary the paper supplies by accident: the capability cost is a curve with a model-dependent floor, so a bigger model steered with the same recipe is not the cheaper edit, and reporting an effect at its best layer without the size-matched MMLU cost is reporting half a result.
- **Pattern:** **The same likelihood instrument that the paper uses to indict steering is what validates it where the concept is real: steering with a Gemma-2-2B Gemmascope French feature leaves a Dutch passage with the largest loss increase and a French passage with the largest loss decrease, as a language feature should, while steering at strength 1 on the practical and safety targets raises perplexity in almost every target-by-behaviour cell and improves none on the model-written question set.** Read against run 2611.07876 (a probe whose pooled AUROC was a difficulty classifier detectable by deleting the response) and run 2605.01699 (a matched non-target null that turned a 0.9 read-out into a statement about a probe), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps finding that the decisive control is the one that asks whether the intervention has the effect the concept implies on text where nobody is measuring the task, and this entry is the cleanest instance because the sanity case and the indictment use one instrument.** Mechanical rule for us: **a direction, feature or ablation our model publishes is run through a likelihood-based effect profile on held-out natural text - the top-increase and top-decrease passages are printed and must be legible under the concept - and a target whose profile shows no cell of measurable benefit is reported as an edit that trades probability between questions rather than one that adds anything, because "it steers the behaviour" and "it promotes the concept" are separated by that profile and by nothing cheaper.**
- **Pattern:** **Steering is reversible by construction here, not by adversary: because the intervention loosens what the model would otherwise select, EPO finds reflective preambles that invert a steered answer at cross-entropy around 5.13 to 5.49 - high enough that the authors call the attack a demonstration rather than a practical threat - and the paper ranks that risk below its own out-of-distribution null.** Read against run 2606.27091 (a fine-tune whose inherited route is inverted by alias variants while the evidence stays intact) and run 2505.03189's own OOD result, the recurrence is that **the folder has two entries now in which the internal signal is present and the behavioural use of it is what breaks, and in both the cheap attack costs nothing on the model side.** Mechanical rule for us: **any intervention our white-box model proposes as a control point is given an invertibility estimate before it is credited - a search over natural prompt prefixes that flips the steered outcome, and the cross-entropy at which such a prefix is found - because an edit that is cheap to apply and cheap to invert moves the deployed model's behaviour without changing what it computes, and the difference between a control and a reversible nudge is exactly that number.**

- **Pattern:** **The base-versus-fine-tune differential is the pile's cleanest instrument for separating inherited structure from learned semantics, and it produces a result that inverts the usual reading of an accuracy gain: Foundation-Sec beats its own parent by 4.7 points (100% vs 95.3%) while its patching effect on a comparable route is SMALLER (−3.82 vs −5.45) and its mean malicious logit margin is lower (3.75 vs 8.15), because fine-tuning concentrated an inherited route into fewer heads rather than building a stronger one - and that concentration is exactly what the evasion variants then break.** Read against run 852 (a represent-versus-act split that had to be inferred across models) and run 856 (a "vs an untrained model of the same architecture" control described in prose but never measured), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps wanting a same-architecture, same-tokenizer, differently-trained contrast and keeps having to approximate it; here the pair is natural and free.** Mechanical rule for us: **whenever our white-box model reports that a fine-tune or a distillation improved fidelity, the entry must print the intervention effect on both the tuned and the untuned model at the same site, because an accuracy rise with a shrinking causal effect is the signature of a narrowed rule and not of a better model - and the pair (accuracy up, effect down) is a two-number verdict that a single benchmark cannot express.**
- **Pattern:** **The most portable method in this paper is an ablation sign test, and its value is that it runs on clean canonical inputs before any adversarial example exists: mean-ablating the canonical Invoke-WebRequest tokens RAISES the fine-tuned model's malicious confidence (+1.13 logit-diff, 73.7% of scripts positive) while the base model drops (−1.60), so the token has changed from a driver to a suppressor, the fine-tune is classifying that family through surrounding payload context, and every one of the four alias variants then fails - the prediction came from the sign of a one-pass ablation, not from a search.** Read against run 851 (a probe at 100% dismantled by regressing out provenance) and run 854 (a flow whose whole argument was that no single vector suffices), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps finding cheap diagnostics that beat expensive ones, but only when the diagnostic is an inter*vention* rather than a read-out - a probe at 100% was worthless here and a sign flip from a single ablation was decisive.** Mechanical rule for us: **our model's published features carry a directed test, not just a decodability score - ablate the feature and sign the change in the target score - and a feature whose ablation moves the target the wrong way is reported as a suppressing rule, because "the model uses this token" and "the model uses this token the way a human would" are separated by that sign and by nothing cheaper.**
- **Pattern:** **Evasion here is signal reversal rather than deletion, and the paper localises the reversal to a boundary instead of a component: on the alias variants the validated late bundle still responds to the malicious content (4/4 still flip under patching) while feed-forward computation before the Layer 13 residual reverses its contribution, so the internal evidence is intact and its use is inverted - and because the two models share a tokenizer, the case-mutation misses cannot be tokenisation artefacts and must come from how the fine-tune reshaped the MLP's treatment of those embeddings.** Read against run 858 (a trained method that put every held-out sequence on the wrong side of its own decision boundary) and run 850 (a complement arm that moved the number downward rather than acting as a null), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps encountering preserved evidence with reversed use, and keeps needing to name the stage where the flip happens because "the representation is wrong" and "the read-out of a right representation is wrong" prescribe different repairs.** Mechanical rule for us: **every failure our model explains is classified at one of three stages - evidence absent, evidence present but the read-out wrong, evidence present but out-weighted downstream - and the stage is pinned by showing the upstream intervention still works while the downstream one has flipped sign, because the middle case is the one that makes a predictive surrogate necessary and the paper's own localisation (late attention works, pre-boundary MLP inverts) is the template.**

- **Pattern:** **The dramatic version of every result in this paper was the wrong one, and each dramatic version had a named control that slew it: full-residual patching "restored refusal to 100%" until patching the mean benign residual at the same site also hit 100%; the onset projection "showed the refusal decision displaced" (2.80 to 0.22) until a benign non-affirmative prefix drove it lower still (−0.82); the "separate refusal feature" reading (cosine about 0.1) did not survive a decorrelated 2x2; and the steering sweep produced 83% restoration at 40% benign over-refusal, a null rather than a win.** Read against run 857 (an 8.3% false-assertion rate reported against a pre-registered 5% tolerance) and run 851 (a 100% probe dismantled by one regression), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps finding that the first, largest, most publishable-looking number is an artefact of a confound the author can name in one sentence, and the paper's real contribution is the ledger of demotions.** Mechanical rule for us: **our white-box model ships a verdict column per claim - passed, demoted, null, retracted - alongside the control that could have killed it, and the entry reports the count of non-passed verdicts as a headline number, because a paper whose controls all pass has either a very narrow claim or a weak control set, and this one prints the ratio (about a third) that makes its passing claims readable.**
- **Pattern:** **Decodability and computation are separated here by an instrument the folder has not used: a difference-of-means injection restored 47% refusal in the instruct model and looked like an active safety mechanism, but a frozen-residual path patch routing only the early MLP - every other activation held at its clean value, bit-exact under a sham/faithfulness/locality unit suite - strips prefill-specific compliance in the base model as hard as in the instruct (−25 vs −21 pp against matched −7/−5) while producing no safety-specific refusal pull at all (concentration 0.007 vs 0.001).** Read against run 852 (a probe whose depth gradient, not its peak, separated computed from surface) and run 849 (a transplant that pinned the stage by holding the basis fixed), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps needing an arm where the *behavioural gap* is removed from the comparison, because a model with a bigger gap will show a bigger intervention effect whether or not it computes anything.** Mechanical rule for us: **any claim that our model contains a task-specific mechanism is tested on a model of the same family that lacks the task, and the mechanism is only credited if the intervention effect survives there in reduced but non-zero form - because "instruct is bigger than base" is a statement about the behavioural gap, and "instruct and base both move, and only instruct routes the freed probability to the task output" is a statement about the computation.**
- **Pattern:** **State is a usable handle where a direction is not, and the paper measures the gap twice: a single harm direction restores refusal 48% against 14% for a random control (real but partial, a third to a half matched by the control) and fails as a global write-handle (58% harmful at 40% benign), while injecting the full mean residual difference between the plain and the attacked run restores 74% held-out against 0% for a matched-norm random vector with a +57 pp selectivity gap.** Read against run 854 (a normalising flow whose whole argument was that no single vector suffices) and run 855 (fidelity near-perfect at exactly the layers where the read-out carried nothing), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps proving single directions insufficient and then having no fallback that is still compact, and here the fallback is a state shift over a short position window rather than a vector over all positions.** Mechanical rule for us: **when our model's published direction fails as an intervention, the entry reports the residual-state arm at the same site before declaring the mechanism unreachable - because "steering does not work" and "steering the wrong object at the wrong site does not work" are different findings, and the site comparison here (response-only 48%/12% against all-positions 58%/40%, same direction, same layer) is what turns the second into the first.**

- **Pattern:** **The paper measures the ceiling and the method on the same axis and the gap is the finding: per-example oracle layering is worth 55% on Llama and 86% on Qwen, the learned router captures a sliver, and the authors defend the sliver with a second measurement - the second- and third-most-steerable layers still beat the fixed baseline while the fourth does not, so the target is a band rather than a point.** Read against run 853 (a penetration threshold whose meaning was never shown to transfer) and run 847 (an anticipatory score printed beside its at-event ceiling), the recurrence is that **the folder's input-conditional and per-unit claims keep being reported without the oracle arm, and here the oracle arm shows that a method which recovers far less than half of the available headroom is still a real gain - because the quantity being predicted is not one point but a neighbourhood.** Mechanical rule for us: **every per-input routing, selection or prediction our white-box model publishes is reported against the per-input oracle on the same held-out split, and the method's capture rate is stated as a fraction of that oracle rather than as a delta over the constant baseline - because \"beats fixed by 19%\" and \"captures 19% of a 55% oracle\" are the same sentence in a table without the ceiling, and only the second tells a reader whether the routing signal is nearly absent or nearly complete.**
- **Pattern:** **Two columns of the same result disagree in magnitude and the paper prints both: Llama truthfulness with L2S goes 0.886 -> 3.175 on the steerability slope while the proportion of steerable examples goes 0.638 -> 0.647, and Llama safety with CAA goes -0.045 -> 0.857 on the slope with 0.477 -> 0.559 on the proportion.** Read against run 852 (a pooled mean over strata that contained both a large effect and no effect) and run 846 (a tier ranking set by a metric invariant to the tier in question), the recurrence is that **the folder's steering wins keep being a large movement of a continuous score accompanied by a small movement in how many units respond at all, and the slope is the metric that most easily grows without the population changing.** Mechanical rule for us: **an intervention our model reports carries both its dose-response slope and the fraction of units that respond in the correct direction, and when the slope moves by an order of magnitude and the fraction moves by a point, the entry says so in the same sentence - because a steeper line fitted through the same set of responders is a fact about the multiplier grid, and any deployment decision that depends on how often steering works is invisible to the slope.**

- **Pattern:** **The validation metric here is measured along the very direction the training loss was built to lengthen, and it says so by saturating: Fisher discriminability rises from 0.39-0.74 in raw space to 0.94-1.00 in the learned space on all thirty model-task pairs, so the check that is offered as evidence of \"better geometry\" cannot rank any two of those pairs.** Read against run 853 (an effective-rank predictor at minus 0.793 that fell to 0.17 once the perturbation norm was partialled out) and run 846 (a ranking blind to the tier carrying most of the variance), the recurrence is that **the folder's diagnostic statistics keep being computed with the answer already baked into their construction, and a score that hits its ceiling everywhere is the tell.** Mechanical rule for us: **any geometry or separability score our white-box model reports is computed along a direction *not* chosen by the same objective - held out, or fitted on a disjoint split of pairs - and a score whose spread across units collapses toward its bound is published as a pass/fail gate rather than as a ranking, because a near-1.0 on every unit is a statement about the fitting procedure and not about the units.**
- **Pattern:** **The zero-strength round trip is the cheapest control in the paper and the only one that separates the two costs: applying the learned map forward and back with no latent shift moves MMLU from 45.35 to 44.90 on LLaMA-3-3B, while actually steering drops it to 42.37 - so roughly 0.45 points are the map and 2.5 are the intervention.** Read against run 850 (a subspace restoring most of the clean-corrupted gap, where the complement's 0% was the number that mattered) and run 849 (a dictionary-vs-inference decomposition that needed the oracle arm to attribute error), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps needing an *identity* arm to make an ablation interpretable, and here the invertible architecture makes that arm exact rather than approximate.** Mechanical rule for us: **every learned transformation our model inserts into a forward pass is measured at strength zero as a first-class result, with the downstream capability delta reported separately from the steered delta - because "invertible" and "lossless" are different claims, the identity path can still cost accuracy through numerical round-trip and normalisation mismatch, and only the zero-strength number tells a reader which part of a later degradation belongs to the tool and which to the edit.**

- **Pattern:** **The category ladder and the null are the same instrument here: safety prompts reach 7.3% of layers, minimal prompts 4.9%, and the difference is reported as a Wilcoxon p of exactly 1.000 - so the paper's strongest negative result is a control that the authors had every incentive to fold into the headline and instead printed as indistinguishable from doing nothing.** Read against run 851 (a probe whose 100% accuracy collapsed to chance once provenance was regressed out) and run 847 (a depletion effect that held in four of five models and failed outright in the fifth), the recurrence is that **the folder's most useful entries are the ones where the *baseline condition* is treated as a rival explanation rather than a floor, and where a null result (p = 1.000) is allowed to sit beside a significant one (p = 0.010) in the same sentence.** Mechanical rule for us: **every "our explanation captures X" claim our white-box model makes is printed with the matched baseline in the same table row and the test between them named - and when the baseline wins or ties, that row is written as a tie rather than omitted, because "safety instructions change as much as the empty string" is the single most informative sentence in this paper and it is invisible to any table that reports only the significant contrasts.** A second, quieter lesson: their behavioural effect size is one minus ROUGE-L, so a shallow prompt that changes only wording scores as much effect as one that changes the computation - text similarity is not behaviour, and our own outcome measures need the same care.
- **Pattern:** **The proof earns its place empirically: CKA deviation is shown to be second-order in the perturbation norm with first-order terms cancelling exactly, and the data bear it out - effective rank looks like a strong predictor of penetration at minus 0.793 until the perturbation's Frobenius norm is controlled, at which point the partial correlation falls to 0.17.** Read against run 846 (a ranking blind to the translation tier that carried most of the variance) and run 844 (a structure whose stability was an artefact of averaging over the units), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps discovering that a distance or similarity statistic is invariant to, or quadratic in, the very quantity it is being used to measure, and here the invariance is stated as a theorem before the experiment confirms it.** Mechanical rule for us: **whenever our model scores a change with a normalized similarity - CKA, RDM correlation, cosine of centred matrices, silhouette - we publish the analytic order of that metric in the perturbation magnitude alongside the measured curve, and any predictor built on such a score is re-fit with the raw norm partialled out before it is reported as a distinct finding, because rank, entropy and every other scale-free statistic will look causal until magnitude is subtracted from underneath it.**

- **Pattern:** **The attack here is on the direction of the usual inference, and the instrument is a confidence-interval rule rather than a significance test: the same direction recovers honouring from 0.57-0.65 to 0.85-0.98 on three models with disjoint bootstrap intervals and moves it 0.04 inside overlapping intervals on the other three, and both blocks are printed in one table, so the honest reading is that the recovery is real only where there was a gap to close.** Read against run 848 (a 2x2 of decode and steer counted across 72 instances) and run 843 (a specificity ratio that separated a steerable from an unsteerable direction), the recurrence is that **the folder's steering results keep being reported as a mean over a population that contains both a large effect and no effect, and the population split is the finding.** Mechanical rule for us: **every intervention our white-box model reports is scored per model and per stratum with intervals, and the headline is the *count* of strata whose intervals are disjoint from baseline rather than the pooled mean shift - because a pooled 0.65-to-0.90 average is what three models at 0.98 and three models at ceiling look like, and a reader given only the average will attribute power to every model in the sweep.**
- **Pattern:** **The decisive check is a leaked version of the same experiment: the probe run with lexically distinct prefixes hits 1.00 at every layer including the earliest, and it is the depth gradient in the clean run (0.74 at layer 6, 0.94 at 18, 1.00 at 24) that separates a computed feature from a surface one, not the peak.** Read against run 851 (a 100% probe dismantled by regression) and run 838 (a readability score that vanished at a stronger decoder), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps needing a *contrast* to make a high number mean anything, and the contrast that works is the deliberately broken version of one's own design rather than a general-purpose null.** Mechanical rule for us: **every probe or decoder our model publishes ships with a deliberately leaked twin - same pipeline, the surface leak re-opened - and the claim is carried by the gap between the twins at the earliest layer, because a peak score with no leak baseline cannot distinguish a computed feature from the wording of the prompt, and a flat-high leak twin beside a rising clean twin is a one-line figure that settles it.**
- **Pattern:** **Two controls are run against the same steering result and only one of them passes cleanly: the learned direction is near-orthogonal to the opener-token unembedding axis (absolute cosine at most 0.14) and to the reply-fitted behaviour axis (cosine 0.09-0.13 against a random maximum of 0.09), while the same direction on a second intent fails the random-direction test outright (separation 6 and 11 against random maxima 19 and 16) - so specificity is reported per intent contrast, not once for the method.** Read against run 844 (a matched-site transplant that flipped a peak-effect win) and run 845 (a third confirmation that a single fitted linear object is a projection of the mechanism), the recurrence is that **the folder's handles keep being certified by an experiment that could not have failed and then generalised beyond it, and here the certificate is refused on the axis it was not run on.** Mechanical rule for us: **a steering direction our model publishes is certified separately on each behaviour axis it is claimed for, and any axis where the norm-matched random control is not beaten is written down as a null rather than folded into a method-level claim - because "specificity holds on this contrast" is a fact about the contrast, and the axis where it does not hold is the one that tells the reader what entanglement looks like in our space.**

- **Pattern:** **This is the folder's first entry where a failure is localised by transplanting *one* component across the two competing pipelines and the transplant is null: SAE encoder, FISTA on the same frozen SAE decoder, and FISTA warm-started from the SAE code all sit at 0.15-0.4 MCC, while the method that learns its own dictionary reaches 0.75-0.95 - so "the decoder is weak" is refuted by holding the basis fixed and the basis is convicted instead.** Read against run 844 (matched-site CAA transplant flipping a peak-effect win) and run 843 (a specificity ratio computed before the intervention), the recurrence is that **the folder's diagnoses are only ever as good as the component it pins down, and a properly pinned diagnosis has the shape "swap X, hold everything else, see nothing move".** Mechanical rule for us: **when our white-box model attributes an error to a stage, it ships the transplant that pins the stage - the strongest available alternative solver dropped onto the same learned basis - and if the alternative does not move the number, the basis is the defendant and no amount of solver engineering gets reported as progress.** The corollary the paper makes explicit and we should adopt in words: the end-to-end score alone cannot distinguish "wrong atoms" from "right atoms, wrong selection", so the ladder (cosine to ground truth, then support precision/recall, then recovery) is the *minimum* for a claim about where the error lives.
- **Pattern:** **The paper treats a benchmark win and an identifiability collapse as two different facts and refuses to let one stand for the other: DL-FISTA beats everything on the probe task (95.79 vs 95.62 raw probe vs 94.63 Top-K, Gemma-2-2B L12) while the same linear probe's recovery of the true latents collapses to MCC below 0.1 at 10,000 latents with per-feature AUC still around 0.93.** Read against run 848 (a 2x2 where steering and decoding are counted separately) and run 847 (an anticipatory score printed beside its at-event ceiling), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps needing two numbers where the field publishes one, and the second number is always the one that says whether the first means anything.** Mechanical rule for us: **every downstream-task accuracy our model reports for a representation is accompanied by a latent-recovery score for that same representation and a named ceiling, because a probe supervised on the target will keep its accuracy while the representation underneath it stops tracking anything - and a supervised probe is exactly the "baseline" our model is usually compared against.**

- **Pattern:** **The same claim is run twice here and the two runs disagree, which is the entry's value: at the anticipatory position the switch signal is decodable out of category in Gemma-9B at AUC 0.72 (layer 26) while at the event position it is 0.87 (layer 16) - i.e. the state at the switch itself describes the decision far better than any state before it** - and the layer curves are flat-to-banded where the event curve peaks in the middle. Read against run 838 (readability and leverage anti-correlated over CoT positions) and run 841 (a stage acquitted by proof, so the remaining freedom localises the cause), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps reading a late, post-decision state as though it were an anticipatory plan, and here the two positions are measured with the same instrument on the same events and are plainly different objects.** Mechanical rule for us: **every read-out our white-box model publishes declares its position relative to the event it is supposed to predict - pre-event, at-event, or post-event - and when a claim is anticipatory, the at-event score is printed beside it as the ceiling, because a 0.87 at the decision point next to a 0.72 before it means most of what looks like foresight is the event explaining itself.**
- **Pattern:** **The paper's central contrast is a within-paper null that the data could easily have lost, and the losing model is reported rather than dropped: the depletion effect holds against depleting the raw category pool in four of five models, and Qwen-7B fails outright at its strongest-effect bin (F 6.139, p 0.061) with three of its five depth bins non-significant.** Read against run 839 (a difference-in-differences interaction score that only survives because its marginals are subtracted) and run 840 (a comparison that reverses sign with the threshold it is read at), the recurrence is that **the folder's predictive claims keep being salvaged by the right baseline being run per model rather than pooled, and here the pooled headline (correlations −0.31 to −0.50, all p below 0.0001) is compatible with a model in which the representational depletion adds nothing over simply running out of animals.** Mechanical rule for us: **any "the model's internal state is running low on X" claim our model makes is scored against the ground-truth depletion of X in the same state, per model, per layer band, with the count of models that lose the contrast named - because a representation that merely mirrors the world it is describing is not a representation of anything the network adds, and only the paired contrast separates the two.**
- **Pattern:** **The generic switching direction is validated against a perturbation that cannot contain the signal under test, and it is the control that draws the map: steering Gemma-9B at layer 26 takes the switch rate from 0.29 to 0.70 positive and 0.07 negative while the norm-matched orthogonalised random vector over the whole layer sweep lands between 0.26 and 0.42, and the same tables show the effect collapsing at the top of the network (layer 40: 0.29 steered against 0.29 baseline) despite a positive-steering p of 1.98E-04.** Read against run 844 (a matched-site transplant that turned a *location* claim into a fitting-tool claim) and run 834 (a format change moving tokens without moving the concept), the recurrence is that **the folder's steering results are only as good as the noise arm, and here the noise arm is strong enough that the residual signal is credible yet narrow banded.** Mechanical rule for us: **every steering result we publish carries a per-layer curve of the orthogonalised, norm-matched random control beside the steered curve, and any layer where steered and noise overlap is drawn as a null even if the significance test calls it significant - because the layer-40 row above passes its test and means nothing, and a reader shown only the star would attribute power to a depth that has none.**

References skimmed.
- **Pattern:** **This is the folder's first entry where the presumed workhorse of an intervention class is invisible to the instrument that ranks the explanation, and the paper states the blindness rather than the result: pure translation takes the largest share of explained variance at every layer on all six prompt-pair groups (`F_T > F_L > F_Ou > F_Oa ~ F_N`), yet translation and uniform-scaled rigid maps are deliberately omitted from the causal geometry panel because the RDM-correlation and silhouette metrics are invariant to them - while translation alone already steers behaviour substantially.** Read against run 840 (a compactness comparison whose sign reversed with the faithfulness target) and run 834 (a format change that moved the tokens without moving the concept), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps discovering that its headline metric family is blind to the transformation it is trying to describe, and here the blindness is structural - the ranking of tiers by geometry is an artefact of distance-based scoring, not a finding about the model.** Mechanical rule for us: **every decomposition our white-box model publishes states, per component, whether the evaluation metric is invariant to that component (translation-invariant metrics under a mean shift, rank-invariant metrics under a rotation, sign-invariant metrics under a polarity flip), and any component the metric cannot see is reported in a separate column rather than ranked inside the table - because a component can carry most of the variance and most of the behaviour and still come last in a well-specified ranking, and a reader who is not told the metric's invariances will read that rank as evidence of unimportance.**
- **Pattern:** **The ceiling is measured, not assumed, and it is cheap: substituting prompt B's own held-out hidden state into prompt A's context at the same layer and token bounds what any single-layer fitted map can recover, and because that context keeps A's prompt tokens and A's attention pattern the bound is strictly below running the model under prompt B end to end.** Read against run 838 (a losing site exonerated by moving the winning vector into it at a fixed norm) and run 826 (a gate certified by a zero-side-effect profile), the recurrence is that **the folder's intervention studies keep reporting recovery without a stated maximum, so an imperfect map and an impossible site are the same number in the table.** Mechanical rule for us: **every recovery or restoration number our model reports carries the oracle-patch ceiling computed on the same site and the same held-out stimuli, printed beside it, so that "the map recovers most of the effect" can be distinguished from "this site could not have delivered the effect even with the target state handed to it".**
- **Pattern:** **The nested-chain increment is the accounting form the folder needs, and its honesty is built in: each tier is scored only by what it adds over its predecessor on held-out stimuli, with the nonlinear residual carried as its own term, and the authors note that increments can go negative under cross-validation when a richer class generalises worse.** Read against run 844 (a deployed vector more stable than the edges it was averaged from) and run 842 (a sign-based admissibility filter beating a magnitude ranking at equal K), the recurrence is that **the folder's structural claims are usually argued by comparing whole methods to each other, and this is the cleanest instance of a family of methods compared to itself in a fixed order.** Mechanical rule for us: **when our model offers a hierarchy of explanations (a mean shift, then a direction, then a subspace, then a map), the report gives each level's held-out increment over the previous level plus the residual, in a fixed order, with a negative increment reported as such - because a richer explanation that loses on held-out data is the single most informative row in the table and it is the row a whole-method comparison never produces.**

- **Pattern:** **This is the folder's first entry where the *unit of the intervention* is made per-direction calibrated rather than borrowed from the vector's norm, and the calibration is what does most of the work: with the range clipped, `alpha`-iterative steering recovers from scoring *below* the no-steering baseline on all three bias datasets (48.0 / 47.0 / 43.5) to scoring 59.0 / 81.0 / 54.0, i.e. the standard method is not weak, it is being run at a strength that was never checked.** Read against run 833 (a paper whose chosen stopping step turned out to be a function of dataset size) and run 830 (three refusal vectors whose cosines ranged over a factor of four at the same nominal construct), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps finding its interventions mis-scaled, and here the mis-scaling is silent because every method reports a dimensionless strength whose meaning differs per direction.** Mechanical rule for us: **every intervention our white-box model reports is expressed in fractions of that direction's own measured usable extent (the interval containing zero that spans the curve's extremes with the steepest monotone segment), never in raw multiples of the contrast norm, and the extent itself is reported as a number - because an unclipped sweep and a clipped sweep of the same vector on the same data are the difference between "this handle does not work" and "this handle works well".**
- **Pattern:** **The geometric fix buys excursion and costs peak, and the paper says so: orthogonalised parameterized steering roughly doubles the controllable range across correlated trait pairs (3.221 and 3.511 against 1.550 and 1.794 for plain `alpha`-iterative) while the un-orthogonalised curve reaches a higher maximum on the power/coordination pair, and at the `beta = +1` extreme the orthogonal arm's gain over its own non-orthogonal version is only 0.472.** Read against run 840 (a compactness comparison whose sign reversed with the faithfulness target) and run 844 (a deployed vector more stable than the edges it was averaged from), the recurrence is that **the folder's structural improvements keep paying out on one axis of the outcome curve and not the other, and the honest entries are the ones that print both axes.** Mechanical rule for us: **any structural change our model makes to a handle (orthogonalise, sparsify, re-centre, average) is reported against the unchanged handle on both the excursion statistic and the peak statistic, because a change that widens the usable band while lowering its ceiling is a different product, and a single "better on range" column would hide exactly the case here where the rival wins the picture.** (Marked as second of two: the peak claim is read from the figure discussion, not from a cell value.)
- **Pattern:** **The paper's own motivating example is the one its method cannot fix, and it localises why in one sentence: after orthogonalisation the warm-and-not-sycophantic quadrant of the projected activation space is still nearly empty of training examples, because the change of basis removes only the linear projection of one direction on the other and the representations overlap in ways that single shared direction does not capture - the warmth score recovers from 26.5 to 43.0 but not to its 61.5 unsteered baseline.** Read against run 843 (a specificity ratio that separated a steerable direction from an unsteerable one) and run 839 (geometry detecting the direct-write subset while missing 88% of strong causal transitions), the recurrence is that **the folder now has a third independent confirmation that a single fitted linear object is a projection of the mechanism, and each confirmation arrives attached to a method that works exactly as designed.** Mechanical rule for us: **when our white-box model publishes a direction or a subspace, the report states which behaviours the object provably cannot separate and why (here: entanglement that is not rank-one overlap), with one measured example - because a method's limits are most credible when demonstrated on the very case that motivated it, and a paper that only exhibits its successes tells us nothing about the failure boundary we will hit.**

- **Pattern:** **The matched-site control is the one that decides, and it decides against the paper's headline on peak effect: CAA placed at CircuitSteer's own layers {6,12,18,24} on Gemma reaches a higher toxicity reduction than the full method (0.232 against 0.113), and the method's entire advantage reduces to the fluency window - matched-layer CAA is valid at 2 of 7 swept coefficients, CircuitSteer at 7 of 7, and on sycophancy matched-layer CAA has no valid point at all.** Read against run 838 (moving the winning vector to the losing site at a fixed norm, which flipped a location claim into a fitting-tool claim) and run 826 (a gate certified by a zero-side-effect profile it could have passed degenerately), the recurrence is that **the folder's head-to-head comparisons keep being decided by which side of the report the control lands on, and the control that matters is always the rival transplanted onto the winner's own ground - here the winner survives, but only because the metric is coverage-under-a-window and not peak effect, and the paper is candid that the peak figure favours the rival.** Mechanical rule for us: **when our model beats a baseline, the headline table also carries the baseline transplanted onto our exact site, depth, or unit set, and if the transplant wins on the metric we chose we either name the second metric that justifies preferring ours (here: the number of valid operating points) or we do not claim the win - because "0.232 beats 0.113" and "7 of 7 beats 2 of 7" describe the same pair of models and only one of them is on our side.**
- **Pattern:** **Every threshold here is swept rather than assumed, and the sweep is made non-vacuous by construction: across all three discovery thresholds on both models the reduction moves by at most 0.044, an order of magnitude below the per-prompt standard deviation (about 0.20 on Gemma, 0.17 on Llama), and the authors prove the instrument can detect a binding threshold by pushing the specificity cutoff to 0.15 on Llama, where the circuit collapses to 6 edges and the reduction falls to 0.032.** Read against run 841 (seven conformance checks that had never once fired and a paper that says so) and run 840 (a compactness claim that reversed sign with the faithfulness target), the recurrence is that **the folder now has a clean template for the robustness section it keeps under-supplying: a plateau plus a deliberate failure at one end, so a flatness claim is not confounded with an insensitive probe.** Mechanical rule for us: **every hyperparameter our model reports a result on ships a sweep with three things named: the range, the largest movement across it, and the size of the per-prompt noise it is being compared against - and where the movement is smaller than the noise we say so in those words rather than writing "stable", because "stable" is what a broken probe also looks like.**
