- **Pattern:** **This is the folder's first pool of directions whose members are not independently fitted but are *paired* by a global coherence constraint, and the ablation says the constraint is doing more work than the choice rule: letting each input pick its own nearest positive and nearest negative centroid - the strictly more adaptive option, over `n_c^2` directions instead of `n_c` - loses to the matched pool on all six models.** Read against run 805 (a matched frozen variant that showed the adaptivity was worth 0.12 points) and run 803 (a per-cluster vector bank with no matched frozen-direction arm at all), the recurrence is that **the folder keeps asking whether conditioning beats averaging, and this entry adds the missing third option: conditioning *within* a globally coherent structure beats both the average and the fully free choice.** Mechanical rule for us: **when our white-box model offers a pool of candidate units or directions and a per-input selector, the pool is built by an explicit global constraint the report names (here: an optimal bijection maximising mutual cosine), and the selector is compared against the unconstrained per-input pairing - because the unconstrained version always looks better motivated and, in this paper, is worse in 6/6, which tells us the win comes from the structure of the pool rather than from the reference to the input.**
- **Pattern:** **The failure mode is named, instrumented, and it is a metric-shopping attractor: steering pushes the model into its most fluent sub-mode of the target concept, which for chat-tuned models is refusal, and refusal is scored as true by the judge, so the headline metric rises while the product metric collapses - on Llama2 7B static per-head steering moves truth 0.937 to 0.957, refusals 0.365 to 0.306, non-informative answers 0.370 to 0.451, and truth-times-info 0.567 to 0.509.** Read against run 807's instruction/concept column trade (an aggregate hiding a component that went backwards) and run 806's capability columns (the headline arm at eleven times the perplexity), the recurrence is that **this folder now has four consecutive entries where the winning number on one axis is bought by a categorical collapse on another, and this is the first to report the collapse as a *rate of a specific degenerate output* rather than as a capability score.** Mechanical rule for us: **every intervention our model reports on a concept that can be satisfied by declining ships the rate of its degenerate satisfier (refusal, abstention, boilerplate hedge) as a column beside the target metric, because a product metric only catches the collapse when one factor is honestly scored - and here the truth judge scores refusals as truthful, so the product caught what the primary metric could not.**

- **Pattern:** **This is the folder's first entry where a learned intervention's effect on the circuit is available in closed form before any experiment, and the form is a kernel rather than a vector: the perturbation to an attention logit is exactly a bilinear form in the query and key hidden states through one matrix whose entries depend only on frozen weights and trained factors, so the "direction" being applied changes with the pair of tokens rather than with the prompt as a whole.** Read against run 806 (a per-example re-weighting of somebody else's transport plan) and run 805 (an input-conditioned direction whose adaptivity had to be bought with a quadratic probe), the recurrence is that **the folder now has three consecutive entries whose claim is that the intervention must depend on context, and this is the only one that can say *what function* it is a context-dependent sample of.** Mechanical rule for us: **when our white-box model predicts the downstream effect of an intervention, we prefer the intervention whose analytic first-order form we can write down (an attention-projection edit, a weight fold) over the one whose form we must estimate, because a closed-form perturbation gives a zero-cost prediction target that isolates the model's remaining error from our estimator's — and a bilinear kernel in two token states is the cheapest such target available to us.**
- **Pattern:** **The reported steering gains are entirely concentrated in the concept column while the instruction column goes the other way, and the paper presents the harmonic mean that hides it: AxBench concept score rises from 0.63 to 1.65 on Llama-3.2-3B and 0.74 to 1.42 on Gemma-2-2B while instruction score falls from 1.78 to 1.75 and 1.77 to 1.47, and PersonalityBench - where the target is a trait expressed over long open-ended text rather than a lexical concept - is a flat tie on every one of the six models.** Read against run 806's IF-Act arm (top concept score at eleven times the perplexity) and run 799's two-axis capability finding, the recurrence is that **every entry in this folder that reports an aggregate steering number has an internal trade that the aggregate is designed to suppress, and the tell is a benchmark whose scoring cannot be summarised by a single direction of movement.** Mechanical rule for us: **any steering or editing result our model reports carries the component columns it was aggregated from, and names one benchmark on which the method does *not* win, because a method that raises its target metric while lowering the co-metric is reallocating behaviour rather than adding control - and the aggression/obedience-style capability side-check is the only place in such a paper where that shows up.**
- **Pattern:** **The geometry is reported as a decomposition with a negative control, and the decomposition splits cleanly: position similarity is high for every grouping and barely moves under shuffling, while velocity, acceleration and Menger curvature rise from essentially zero to roughly 0.27-0.39 only when segments are grouped by instruction and only under the original ordering.** Read against run 800's three-intervention-type separation and run 796's site-versus-subspace ablation, the recurrence is that **the folder's geometry claims keep being made about single scalars, and the papers that decompose a trajectory into order statistics find that the low-order quantity is the uninformative one.** Mechanical rule for us: **when our model describes what an intervention did to a representation, it reports the displacement and at least one higher-order trajectory statistic (velocity or curvature) against an order-destroying shuffle, because the shuffle is what tells a real structural effect from a rearrangement, and in this paper the quantity that looked like the primary measurement - position - was the one that could not discriminate.**

- **Pattern:** **The gate is two lines and does more work than the vector: intervene only after the model has already failed once on its own, which needs two stored cluster ids and no learned parameters - and the paper then documents exactly what that gate cannot see, namely whether the third visit is productive or destructive, because the same transition statistics show the last phase is absorbing and nothing stops the controller from pushing a trace there.** Read against run 801 (a cheap screen scored at r = 0.73 against the full grid) and run 798 (a support gate whose removal cost 49 points of cross-task accuracy), the recurrence is that **the folder's most reusable components are always the ones with no learned parameters and an explicit external form, and the paper always finds their blind spot by an ablation rather than by argument.** Mechanical rule for us: **every gate our white-box model ships declares the event it conditions on, the quantity it cannot see, and the absorbing state it might push an input into - because a gate that fires on repetition is a statement about history, not about whether the next repeat will be helpful, and in this paper the trace's own dynamics (dwell 0.937-0.955, one absorbing terminal phase) are what the gate is blind to.**
- **Pattern:** **The metric is the intervention's own target event and the authors say so in the limitations: a loop-exit rate certifies that a state changed and nothing about whether the trace improved, with no accuracy and no token count anywhere in the paper.** Read against run 797 (a generation-length ablation as a side measurement) and run 800 (a subspace whose transfer was read at or below chance), the recurrence is that **this folder now has several entries where the headline number is definitionally aligned with the method's own hypothesis, and the papers that survive scrutiny are the ones that publish the number that is not aligned.** Mechanical rule for us: **every intervention we report ships the target event it was built to move beside one measured quantity it was not built to move, because a method can win its own metric in every cell while the trace it edited is no better than the one it did not - and if that second number was not measured, that absence is the finding to record.**

- **Pattern:** **The sign of the intervention is measured, not assumed: whether to steer toward or away from refusal comes from a probe threshold chosen to maximise a balanced criterion on a held-out ROC, which is the explicit pole-fixing rule run 801's gap asked for - and the paper then shows the unmeasured version failing, since adding a logit bias on the same token flips the first token only and the model goes on to refuse anyway.** Read against run 801 (directions whose positive end was decided by the pooled data, producing a "skill" axis that turned out to be labelled speculative reasoning) and run 796 (a unit chosen by its read score and used to write), the recurrence is that **this folder keeps buying unsupervised geometry precisely to avoid declaring a premise, and every time the premise comes back it comes back as an unargued label or a default positive end; here it comes back as a *calibrated* threshold instead.** Mechanical rule for us: **every steering claim our model reports names the statistic that fixes the pole (which measured quantity counts as "more of the property"), the held-out set it was calibrated on, and the sign-dependent claim in terms of the pole rather than the coordinate - and a purely token-level intervention is reported next to a representation-level one at the same strength, because this paper's logit bias shows a fix that influences one token and leaves the representation untouched.**

- **Pattern:** **This is the folder's cleanest case of the same quantity being ranked two ways and only one ranking being causal - the property is linearly decodable from a broad set of heads while only a few write strongly onto it, so a probe-based selection (ITI) detects widely and steers badly, and an explained-variance selection steers well.** Read against run 796's predecessor 795 (a steering-cost matrix that had to choose between a dictionary and an empirical second moment, both of which weight directions) and run 789 (the ViT counting entry where decodability and patch effect crossed), the recurrence is that **every entry in this folder that has scored a unit by how well it *reads* a property has then used that score to choose a unit to *write* into, and the two rankings agree less often than the field assumes.** Mechanical rule for us: **every unit our white-box model ranks for intervention ships both scores at the same coordinate - a read score (probe accuracy, explained variance of a projection) and a write score (how much of that unit's output lands on the target readout) - and the intervention set is drawn from the write ranking with the read ranking reported beside it, because a unit that decodes the property from everywhere and writes it from nowhere is the modal case, not an edge case.**

- **Pattern:** **The output vocabulary is used here as a free dictionary of directions and the transfer is entirely in *where* it is read: pushing the unembedding columns back through the head's own output matrix and a linearised RMSnorm converts a residual-stream direction into a raw-head-space direction, so the same atoms serve head selection (through the reconstruction residual) and steering (through the projection) with one calibration pass and no training.** Read against run 794 (a predictor built from decoder geometry with zero forward passes) and run 781 (a matched-null suite that established a signal was not generic), the recurrence is that **the folder's cheapest weight-side objects - unembedding columns, output matrices, norm gains - are sufficient to build both a selector and an intervention in head space, and the cost is one matrix multiply and one pass over a small calibration set.** Mechanical rule for us: **every per-unit analysis in our white-box model starts from its readout geometry (the composition of the unit's write map with the final norm and the unembedding) before any activation is collected, because that matrix alone gives a per-unit dictionary, a read score and a projection operator, and activation-side analysis should be justified as adding something the geometry cannot.**

That is exactly the predictive claim a white-box model should make, and it is one experiment away here. The successor is a paper that, from the SAE's decoder geometry alone, predicts the **side-effect profile** of steering a given feature — or, failing that, one that tests the co-recruitment mechanism by measuring off-target movement as a function of neighbour cosine. A second and cheaper successor, closer to our own need: this paper's ranking signal is weight-static, so nothing here says whether geometry predicts the cost of an intervention **applied at a different site** (an MLP output rather than the residual, a head rather than a feature) — a cross-site transfer test that would tell us whether decoder crowding is a property of the dictionary or of the network.

- **Pattern:** **This is the folder's first entry that reports the perturbation magnitude of every intervention beside its effect at the level of the residual vector itself - cosine above 0.999 and norm change under one per cent, on fewer than twenty of 768 dimensions - and the reason it matters is that the same paper's own (9,6) result shows an effect that moves the wrong way in proportion to the intervention: a local ablation lowers that head's attention score and raises the indirect-object logit by an amount that tracks how far the score fell.** Read against run 783 (an ablation judged causally effective while the residual cosine stayed near 0.99, used then as a licence) and run 790 (a full-residual ceiling used as a denominator), the recurrence is that **this folder has been using "the edit was small" as a claim about the edit's legitimacy, and this paper shows the smallness says nothing about the direction of the downstream consequence - a tiny subspace edit on one head can be locally correct and globally backwards.** Mechanical rule for us: **every intervention our white-box model reports ships three numbers, not two - effect on the target quantity, effect on the model's answer, and the edit's magnitude - and any case where the first and second have opposite signs is published as a dissociation rather than averaged into an aggregate, because in this paper that one inverted head is the only evidence that the three name-movers are not interchangeable.**
- **Pattern:** **Redundancy is measured here by additivity rather than inferred from preserved accuracy, and the measurement splits cleanly by graph shape: ablating two edges on parallel paths together produces a larger effect than either alone, while ablating edges on serial paths together does not add up.** Read against run 791 (sufficiency at 122 heads and necessity at 250, a factor-of-two gap attributed to redundant pathways that were never measured - this run's named successor) and run 789 (a transport story asserted rather than tested), the recurrence is that **every redundancy claim this folder has read has been an inference from "competence survived", and this paper is the first to turn redundancy into a property of pairs of paths that can be counted.** Mechanical rule for us: **any redundancy our white-box model claims ships a pairwise additivity matrix over the candidate paths - ablating each alone, each pair together, and reporting the superadditivity ratio - because equal to the sum is shared load, above the sum is genuine backup, below the sum is one path feeding the other, and only the first two are redundancy while the third is seriality mistaken for it.**
- **Pattern:** **The trace's own validation is graded and the grade is published in the graph: the most-frequent-edges skeleton recovers eleven of sixteen reachable reference heads at precision about 0.52, and the paper states the ceiling explicitly - only sixteen of the reference circuit's heads can even appear, because the trace starts from three seeds.** Read against run 785 (a feature/residual share table summing to the explained quantity) and run 788 (a matched-operating-point comparison stated per benchmark), the recurrence is that **this folder keeps scoring circuit recovery as precision and recall against a published circuit without stating which part of the reference was reachable from the seeds, so a recall of 0.69 and a recall of 1.0 look different when they may be the same.** Mechanical rule for us: **every agreement score our model reports against an external reference ships its reachable denominator (seeds, cutoffs, unit alphabet) alongside the F1, because precision and recall against an unreachable target are not measurements of the method - and the deleted-and-therefore-missing part is itself a finding about which edges the sparsity rule costs.**

- **Pattern:** **This is the folder's first entry that separates the three things an attention head does - what it reads (keys/values), what it asks (query), and what it writes (output) - into three independent transplants on the same head set, and the separation is what turns a localisation into an algorithm: the output transplant is what *finds* the 122 heads, the key/value swap on the task span is what shows the heads re-read the goal on every step (94% causal shift), and the query swap at the pivot is what shows those queries carry progress (57% against a 3% random-head null).** Read against run 783 (destination and source interventions on rank-1 signals that could not say whether the moved thing was what the head asked for or what it found) and run 787 (path patching that ranked heads by an attribution score without ever swapping the QK side), the recurrence is that **this folder has been localising units and then making claims about *what travels through* them, and only a read/ask/write split can tell an edge carrying a goal from an edge carrying its syntax.** Mechanical rule for us: **every circuit edge our white-box model reports is decomposed into source-state, query-state and output arms, each transplanted alone and each reported with its own number - because a head whose output transplant redirects the model while its key/value transplant does not is a head that is *causing* the action, and one where only the key/value swap moves the model is a head that is *relaying* the context, and the two are indistinguishable from an output-side attribution score.**
- **Pattern:** **The paper's own strongest claim is falsified-in-part by its own control, and the shape of the dissociation is the transferable lesson: sufficiency is near-total (keep 122 heads' span access, blind ~93% of heads above layer 19, ability preserved) while necessity requires roughly twice as many (blinding those same 122 leaves competence intact; only the 250-head blinding bites), and the readout budget shows the same slack - 25 heads already read the goal out, more than ~100 adds little, yet interventions need the larger set.** Read against run 781 (a four-arm matched-null suite that made an ablation's claim "these units rather than equally large units in the same places") and run 774 (a granularity ablation where the unit alphabet chose the circuit), the recurrence is that **this folder has been reporting ablation effects as a function of the set size without ever publishing the size at which the effect appears, so a redundant pathway and an inert head both look like a null.** Mechanical rule for us: **any head or unit set our model calls a bottleneck ships a size sweep on both arms - the smallest set whose preservation suffices, and the smallest set whose removal is necessary - and the two numbers are reported as a pair, because a set that is sufficient at 122 and necessary at 250 is a *pathway family*, not a bottleneck, and a single ablation at either size licenses the opposite conclusion.**
- **Pattern:** **The mechanism claim is about absence of state: the paper argues a depth-bounded transformer cannot carry a goal forward for more tokens than it has layers left, then tests not "is the encoding carried" but "what is being re-read", and the contest is decided by a 2x2 transplant where the task span beats the code-progress span even though the progress span demonstrably holds traces of the same operation (traces that only surface when their values are amplified fourfold).** Read against runs 785, 789, 790 (three entries whose decode/patch pairs came apart at a fixed coordinate) and run 783's finding that identical graphs can carry different content, the recurrence is that **this folder keeps finding the same quantity in two places and deciding which is load-bearing by whichever it measured first.** Mechanical rule for us: **when our white-box model reads the same variable at two coordinates, the deciding experiment is a transplant grid over both spans with each held fixed, and the weaker signal is reported with the amplification or denoising needed to see it - because a trace that is present and suppressed and a trace that is absent produce identical readouts and opposite models of where the next action comes from.**

- **Pattern:** **This is the folder's first entry that publishes, as a required field, how many of the *original* units each extracted unit is composed from - and the answer is that roughly half the extracted units are single-source, so half of them a head-level analysis could have found and the other half are exactly the cases where per-head attribution is silently wrong.** Read against run 786 (a theory that is explicitly per-head and names cross-head singular-vector allocation as its own open gap) and run 780 (a local statistic that was a decomposition of the same adjacency as its headline), the recurrence is that **every decomposition this folder has read publishes its units and never publishes their ownership, so the reader cannot tell which claims would survive being re-expressed at the coarser unit.** Mechanical rule for us: **every unit our white-box model publishes carries a composition count - how many of the coarser units it draws its output from, measured by projection onto the coarse basis rather than asserted by the training objective - and any per-unit causal claim is qualified when the composition count exceeds one, because a behaviour split 50/50 across two heads is either halved or double-counted by a per-unit ablation and looks like a weak effect in both cases.**
- **Pattern:** **The second pattern is that the paper defends its residual by comparing it to a *different* decomposition's residual on the same layer, and that comparison is the cheapest evidence available that the unexplained part is a property of the phenomenon rather than of the method: Lorsa's fraction of variance unexplained correlates with a same-size attention SAE's FVU per layer, per token, and in error direction, and both leave a majority of units inactive.** Read against run 785 (an 84%/46% feature-share split inside one pipeline) and run 786 (a residual near-zero by construction that therefore said nothing), the recurrence is that **this folder has been reporting residuals as a property of its own method, and the residual only becomes a fact about the model when an independently parameterised decomposition of the same object leaves a correlated residual.** Mechanical rule for us: **our model's residual ships with a second, differently-parameterised decomposition of the same layer, and the claim that the gap is intrinsic requires the two residuals to correlate per example and in direction - because a residual that is a tuning failure decorrelates from everyone else's, and a residual that is shared is the part of the network no current dictionary shows.**

- **Pattern:** **The ceiling theorem is the folder's first instrument that predicts an accuracy limit from the *task's algebra* before training, and its predictions are exact integers rather than fitted constants: a commutative mechanism is capped at the reciprocal of the commutator subgroup's order (1/2 for $D_4$, 1/4 for $A_4$, 1/12 for $S_4$, 1/60 for $A_5$), a stack of k commutative layers at the reciprocal of the k-th derived subgroup, and the observed learned signature heads land at 0.068-0.091 for $A_4$ against a 1/12 chance and a 0.25 cap.** Read against run 772 (a per-step hazard that makes an aggregate a one-sided bound) and run 770 (an exact closed-form null that made a census readable), the recurrence is that **this folder keeps asking what a model *cannot* do and answering with a null model; this paper answers with a quotient of the task.** Mechanical rule for us: **any mechanism our white-box model proposes is placed in its mechanism class first (commutative, cascaded, signature-like, lookup) and given the pre-computable ceiling for that class on that task, and a result below the ceiling is read as an optimization gap while a result at the ceiling is read as the mechanism, not as a model limitation - because 0.323 against a constructed 1.000 and 0.0168 against a capped 0.0167 are opposite findings with the same architecture.**
- **Pattern:** **The paper gives the folder three *separate* evidence categories that have been conflated in almost every composition result it has read: fit at training lengths, finite evaluation at a stated test length, and an algebraically verified snapped model with a bounded horizon for the raw learned weights - and the gap between the last two is large and quantified (raw horizons 71-276 and 100-222 letters against first observed errors at 7,253-73,076, a factor of 9 to 2,711 with median 201; and one $Q_8$ run that passed length 1,000 failed at 2,000).** Read against run 777 (a 96.9% decode with 0.038 next-hop use) and run 776 (B^D decodable at R^2 1.00 at initialisation), the recurrence is that **a long finite pass is this folder's most common form of evidence and it is systematically weaker than it reads.** Mechanical rule for us: **every long-horizon number our white-box model reports ships its stated test length, a worst-case certified horizon where one can be computed, and the first observed failure on a much longer probe - because "exact to 1,000" and "certified to 71" and "first error at 7,253" are the same model, and reporting only the first is the weakest of the three true statements.**

- **Pattern:** **This is the folder's first entry where a representation is measured at full decodability and simultaneously at zero usefulness, and the paper makes the two a first-class distinction rather than a caveat: an aged entity state still decodes as the right entity at 96.9% argmax while its score for the next relation application is 0.038 against 0.650 for a fresh donor, the receiving position's own decayed state costs the same 0.650 -> 0.057, and a single shared fresh-aged direction moves those numbers to 0.698 and 0.031 without adding any information.** Read against run 776 (a staged intermediate fully decodable at R² 1.00 that the output stream does not read) and run 770's constraint-free point that a component can be in every forward pass without being the mechanism, the recurrence is that **decodability has been this folder's proxy for presence, and presence has now been shown twice in one week to be a different fact from use.** Mechanical rule for us: **every representation our white-box model records carries a separate usability field, measured by a composition test - hand the state to the next stage and check whether the downstream computation proceeds from it - and any claim of the form 'the quantity is available here' is filed as representational until a swap makes the next stage act on it, because a 96.9% decoding accuracy and a 0.038 next-hop score are the same vector.**
- **Pattern:** **The two state swaps are the cleanest two-variable dissociation in the folder so far, because they are cross-factorial rather than ablative: a temporal swap holds example and position fixed and changes only how old the state is, a cross-example swap holds pass and position fixed and changes only whose content it is, and the results separate the entity operand from the relation selection - replacing `[EQ]` makes the model compute the recipient's next relation applied to the donor's entity at 95.2% on an unseen hop while the attention pointer stays on the recipient's own key, and replacing a relation token's state makes the pointer move one key forward while the entity register is untouched.** Read against run 776's three-donor content swap (one route, one factor varied per arm, 100/100/0 source-exact) and run 769's functional-slot ladder, the recurrence is that **the tightest control is now a 2x2 of (which position, which pass) rather than a donor identity, and it buys operand-versus-operation separation that no single-factor swap can.** Mechanical rule for us: **every routing claim our model makes ships both swap arms - same position across passes, and same pass across positions - and the claim names which of the two variables moves the observable, because a route that carries content and a route that carries an index produce identical ablation curves and opposite swap tables.**
- **Pattern:** **The failure analysis gives the folder a reusable decomposition of a long-horizon result into a per-step hazard and a repair term that is measured and found to be zero: after the first intermediate error at n=20 only 2 of 21 trajectories later decode a correct intermediate, 0 of 21 sustain it, and 1 of 21 reaches the correct final answer, while at n=30 all 64 trajectories err, 22 show a transient correct hop, and sustained recovery and post-error correctness are both 0/64 - and the paper's survival identity turns 'accuracy at length' into a product of one-minus-hazard with no independence assumption.** Read against run 772's per-step transition log (a composed map's corruption carried forward by 400+ steps) and run 771's fate-class breakdown (a stable core inside a churning set), the recurrence is that **every long-horizon number in this folder has been an aggregate over steps whose error process was never characterised.** Mechanical rule for us: **any multi-step prediction our model makes is reported as a per-step hazard curve plus the aggregate survival it implies, and where we cannot predict repair we say the aggregate is a one-sided bound - because 'the trajectory usually finishes correctly' and 'nothing repairs a mistake' are compatible with the same final accuracy and imply different things about where additional depth helps.**

- **Pattern:** **This is the folder's first entry that answers the cross-subgraph-traffic question with a single object rather than an intervention: because every component output is additive in the stream and every component reads the stream through a key-value form, credit can be split at each hop across the *entries* and then across the *writers of those entries*, so the "interface" between a mechanism and its complement is not a separate thing to measure - it is the branch label on each hop (K, Q or V) and the entry shares inside it, and the branch label is what recovers a circuit down to the mode a head used, where a single per-component score cannot.** Read against run 774 (a dual-mask fit that partitions a model into a circuit and a complement with no edges and no flow between them) and run 773 (a within/cross partition ratio that decays as the set widens), the recurrence is that **every partition this folder has published is set-theoretic, and the information actually crosses at entries, not at units.** Mechanical rule for us: **any mechanism our white-box model names is accompanied by the entry-level split inside each unit and the branch label on each hop (which input channel the credit travelled), and the mechanism is reported as a set of labelled edges rather than a set of units - because "head A feeds head B" and "A feeds B's query side but not its key side, through source position 2" are different objects, and only the second predicts which intervention moves the behaviour.**
- **Pattern:** **The paper's central finding is a *signature* for the difference the folder keeps running into between contribution and causality, and the signature is a matched counterfactual rather than an ablation: layer-0 components hold high credit on every prompt, task or not, so moving from IOI to the matched ABC prompts where no name repeats leaves their coverage at 100% while the path-patched components lose 30-70 points at layers 2-6 - i.e. the components whose credit is task-tied collapse when the task is removed, and the components whose credit is positional do not.** Read against run 774 (a rate reached by destroying the utility that would separate it from collapse) and run 771 (a partition present at step 0, before training, at multiples of its own substrate), the recurrence is that **a component can be strongly and consistently *part of* every forward pass while being causally irrelevant to the thing being explained, and the diagnostic is whether its credit moves when the task moves.** Mechanical rule for us: **every high-credit unit our model reports is run on a matched counterfactual input that removes the task while preserving surface statistics, and the unit is classified by its coverage drop - task-tied if it collapses, bias-like if it holds - because a prompt-independent component is indistinguishable from a mechanism on any single-prompt reading, and an attribution tool that cannot make that distinction will hand its users the attention sink and the layer-0 writer as the mechanism.**
- **Pattern:** **Both of the paper's wins that survive a harder check are the ones where a *dispatch rule* was chosen against what the gate says, and the ablation makes the size of the difference explicit: splitting credit by attention weight hands position 0 a 28.9% share and top-1 rank on 32% of IOI prompts (22.3% and 18% on factual recall, 9.2% and 4% on general text), while splitting by what the entry actually wrote in the direction the component wrote drops top-1 to 0% on all three sources with no BOS filtering anywhere; and in the faithfulness test the same discipline is what beats a non-negative heuristic by only 0.001 (+0.085 vs +0.084 IFR), so the paper's *headline* margin comes from one metric while its *robustness* margin comes from the dispatch rule.** Read against run 770 (an exact null that made a census readable where a permutation would not) and run 766 (a ranking credited only through the intervention it predicted), the recurrence is that **an attribution's stability comes from where the credit is projected, not from the depth of the recursion or the number of paths enumerated.** Mechanical rule for us: **every credit split our model performs is defined against the direction the unit actually wrote, and any alternative split (gate weight, activation magnitude, norm) is reported as an ablation arm - because the gate tells you what was selected and the projection tells you what was contributed, and the sink is the case where those two disagree most.**

- **Pattern:** **The no-STE row is the folder's cleanest case of a success metric that is indistinguishable from model collapse, and the paper reports it because it happened to print a utility column: without the straight-through estimator the clean subgraph reports 0.0% backdoor ASR - a perfect result - while GSM8K falls from 72.0 to 0.0 and MMLU from 67.2 to 25.9, i.e. the model no longer answers anything, and the authors say so explicitly.** Read against run 766 (an ablation reaching 80% of responses while the *direction* of change was a phrasing swap, so the classifier was the result) and run 765 (a comparative win scored against a baseline run at one eighth of the budget), the recurrence is that **every headline in this folder is a rate on one axis, and a rate can be driven to its ideal value by destroying the thing it measures.** Mechanical rule for us: **every masked, ablated or optimised result our white-box model emits ships a utility benchmark on the same arm as the target rate, and any arm whose utility falls outside a stated band is reported as collapse rather than as an effect - because "ASR 100% -> 0.0%" and "the model outputs nothing" are the same number, and only the second metric separates them.**
- **Pattern:** **The granularity ablation is the strongest evidence in this folder that a circuit's contents are a function of the unit alphabet rather than of the behaviour: the same refusal backdoor on the same model is a 0.42%-sparse neuron set (residual in-domain ASR 0.0%, OOD 0.4%) or a 3.61%-sparse head set (6.6% and 14.4%), and the same alignment behaviour is 3.03% of heads plus 0.79% of neurons (ASR 96.9%) or 8.89% of heads alone (60.2%), with the paper reading all of these as successful attributions of the same thing.** Read against run 773 (a within/cross partition ratio that decays from 5.4x to 1.4x as the set widens, so the partition lives in the ranking's head) and run 771 (a partition measured at one fixed roster size), the recurrence is that **"this unit set implements that behaviour" is always relative to a choice of what a unit is, and every such claim in this folder has been stated at one alphabet.** Mechanical rule for us: **whenever our model reports a unit set as a mechanism, the same discovery procedure is rerun at a coarser and a finer unit alphabet and both sets are published with their residual effects - because two disjoint sets at two granularities are not a robustness result, they are a non-identifiability result, and saying which one we published is the whole of the claim.**
- **Pattern:** **The dual-mask construction is the closest thing in this folder to a composition test, and it is worth stealing on structure rather than on numbers: rather than ranking units and ablating the top-k, it optimises two graphs against each other - a dense complement constrained to reproduce normal behaviour on clean inputs and to neutralise the triggered behaviour on poisoned ones, and a sparse circuit constrained to carry the target behaviour only on triggered inputs - with an explicit overlap penalty keeping the intersection small (91-99% sparse across all three backdoor types).** Read against run 767 (a double dissociation run in both directions, where the shared subgraph was the third arm) and run 759 (where a "removable" set was weakened by a second replacement value), the recurrence is that **the honest way to claim a set carries a function is to make the complement carry everything else, and to penalise their overlap during the fit rather than measuring it afterwards.** Mechanical rule for us: **any partition our white-box model proposes is fitted as a partition - complement constrained to reproduce the residual behaviour, overlap penalised in the objective, and the intersection reported as a sparsity number - because a top-k ranking plus a matched control asks whether the set matters, and a dual-mask fit asks whether the set is the mechanism, and only the second gives the complement a job to do.**

- **Pattern:** **The specificity ladder here is the best-instrumented instance in the folder for a functional-interface claim, because the four controls are not random sets but the *other three things one could have patched at the same interface*: restoring the source key recovers 83-100 percent of the disrupted margin in six settings, while restoring the source value moves it by at most +0.17, restoring an off-site key makes it worse, and patching the query moves it by exactly 0.00 - and the same ladder reappears downstream in the enrichment experiment, where replacing distractor keys removes or introduces the competition failure and replacing values does neither.** Read against run 764 (a random-head floor matched on size and location) and run 751 (a specificity ratio whose matched-random control was the same order as the effect), the recurrence is that **the strength of a causal claim is set by how precisely the control is matched, and the tightest possible match is a different functional slot of the same interface at the same position.** Mechanical rule for us: **whenever we claim a component carries a specific function, the control arm is the same intervention at the neighbouring functional slots (value instead of key, query instead of source, off-site instead of on-site) and not a random set - because "this key matters and that key does not" is a claim about a computation, and "this key matters and random units do not" is a claim about sparsity.**
- **Pattern:** **The horizon result is the one place in this folder where a white-box model derives, from wiring alone, which context a component cannot see, and then measures its own boundary: R_local <= L(W-1) predicts that three sliding-window layers of width 2 cannot carry lag-4 information into the pre-receiver block, and at W=2 in-horizon lag-3 carrying is positive while out-of-horizon lag-4 carrying in that block is identically zero, with wider windows (W in {4,8,16}, R_local >= 9) retaining positive lag-4 effects.** The companion visibility theorem is the same idea in the disambiguation setting - a paired-prompt bound pins accuracy at 1/2 once the identity cue falls outside the writer's radius - and the paper then shows the multi-layer alternative, where adjacent relays compose as S∘S = S^2 so that a richer address is built out of short shifts rather than a wider kernel. - **Pattern:** **This is the folder's first entry where the one thing changed is the scalar at the root of the graph, and it is the cleanest demonstration yet that an attribution pipeline is a function of its target rather than of its tracer: the same Cross-Layer Transcoders, the same Jacobian, the same 80/95 pruning, rooted at a probe direction instead of a logit, yields a graph whose ablation arm flips the token 0% of the time on every concept in both models while the logit-rooted graph on identical prompts flips it 100% (92% for reasoning).** That is a double dissociation in the strict sense, run in both directions with the shared subgraph as the third arm, and the paper does not have to argue that the two graphs are different because it ablates each one against the other's outcome. Read against run 766 (where a ranking was only credited once it predicted the intervention it fed) and run 760 (where the record with the most fields scored second-worst), the recurrence is that **in this folder the target of a reading is an experimental variable that is almost never varied, and varying it is cheaper than any method improvement on top of a fixed target.** Mechanical rule for us: **every attribution or circuit our white-box model emits names its root scalar explicitly, and we run the alternative root (the probe score, the next token, the layer's own output) as a second arm on the same prompts - because a graph that explains the logit and a graph that explains the representation are both true and neither is the model, and only the double ablation tells us which one we published.**

- **Pattern:** **This entry is the folder's first where the winning configuration is measured outside the losing method's feasible range, and the paper says so in a figure caption rather than in the result: LRP's best compression row needs 8,192 reference samples, and Wanda's official implementation "cannot" exceed 1,024 for GPU memory, so the 11.35-perplexity win is scored against a baseline run at one eighth of the budget.** Read against run 758 (a predictive statistic reported with its saturation point, so the reader could see where the fit stopped buying) and run 761 (a method whose gain concentrated entirely in the tasks it was designed around), the recurrence is that **in this folder a comparative headline is usually a comparison of two different experimental budgets, and the budget gap is disclosed somewhere in the appendix.** Mechanical rule for us: **every arm in one of our comparisons is run at the sample budget of the cheapest arm, and any result reported above that budget carries the budget it used in the same cell - because "ours is better when it gets 8x the data" is a sentence about data, and a reader who cannot see the 8x will file it as a sentence about method.**
- **Pattern:** **The most useful negative result here is a null that localises the unit rather than the method: structured pruning of attention heads for IOI fails for LRP, Wanda, gradient and activation alike, while the same four methods succeed on MLP neurons - and the authors read it as OPT-125M's heads cooperating rather than any small subset being dispensable.** That is the folder's clean answer to "what does a method that returns nothing mean": not weak attribution, wrong unit. Read against run 764 (component identity survived fine-tuning while edge wiring subtyped the verdict) and run 760 (all six fields at Bonferroni p = 1.0 on GPT-2 while the CNN arm passed both directions), the recurrence is that **a causal unit menu is an empirical finding, and the test of the menu is whether every method in a panel fails on it together.** Mechanical rule for us: **when our white-box model returns a mirage on one unit type, we do not tune the attribution - we re-run the panel at the coarser unit and report both, because a null shared by four independent rankings is evidence about the substrate, and the entry that reports the null is more predictive than the entry that reports the win.**
- **Pattern:** **Differential attribution is the cheapest editing primitive in the folder and it is a pure double-difference: score every parameter twice, once on references that elicit the behaviour and once on a general corpus, subtract, prune the most negative - with no patching, no fine-tuning, and no forward pass over the target inputs at all.** The cost statement in App. G is what makes it a real option: one forward-backward per reference sample at 5 seconds, and the toxicity arm concentrates on 100 fc1 neurons (0.3%) while repetition needs about 7,000 weight elements (0.03%), so the size of the edit is itself a readout of how concentrated the behaviour is. Read against run 762 (a trainable intervention certified against the untouched model) and run 760 (a vocabulary pivot that moved recovery from 3/16 to 13/16), the distinction is that the trained objects require a behavioural proof to be trusted while a subtraction requires only the reference sets to be right - which is precisely the limitation the authors name and do not solve. Mechanical rule for us: **any contrastive score we emit carries the two reference distributions that produced it, in the record, not in the appendix - because a differential is an assertion about what distinguishes two corpora, and if the benign corpus overlaps the behaviour corpus the score measures the overlap, not the behaviour.**

Read against run 764 (base-vs-instruct, where component identity survived fine-tuning while edge wiring sub-typed the verdict) and run 762 (circuit condensation, where the object was built rather than found and had to answer for the untouched model), the recurrence is that **every circuit in this folder is defined relative to an earlier choice of what counts as a node, and the choice is the assumption that does the work.** Mechanical rule for us: **our white-box model's unit menu is declared before any measurement, and every claim that comes out of it is labelled with what the menu cannot express - because a pipeline that omits a component type is not a partial pipeline, it is a pipeline for a different model, and "preserves 86% of behaviour" on the excluded half is a number about the residue.**
- **Pattern:** **The reduction in this paper is obtained by coarsening the graph before searching it, which is the cleanest statement in this folder of a technique we already half-use: cluster the vertices spectrally at each resolution, replace each cluster with a supernode, and let a learned policy decide which supernodes are worth descending into - so the refinement depth becomes a parameter instead of an implicit property of the method.** The price is stated honestly in Table V and is small: removing the hierarchy takes modular-arithmetic preservation from 0.91 to 0.89 while cutting runtime to 0.3x, meaning most of the coarse structure was recoverable without the ladder, whereas the cross-layer prediction head is what costs quality when removed (0.91 -> 0.84 modular arithmetic, 0.85 -> 0.76 QA). - **Pattern:** **This is the folder's first entry where the circuit is an OBJECTIVE rather than a finding, and the argument structure it introduces is worth more than the result: if the object you want to read cannot be extracted from the frozen model, you may be allowed to build one - provided you then prove the built object still answers for the untouched model, with a behavioural test and not a distributional one.** The proof here is two-layered and the second layer is the interesting one: KL to the original (median 0.215; IOI anchor 0.056 against the matched frozen circuit's 0.50) is the distributional half, and the competence readout - ranking the ORIGINAL model's own errors by the margin read through the condensed circuit, AUROC 0.894 against 0.645 at matched edge budget, ahead in 10 of 11 evaluable cells - is the behavioural half that a re-expressed activation could not pass by accident. Read against run 760 (where the richest record was the second-worst of six and the fix was leave-one-out within the full record) and run 754 (where the method's own justification for corrupting rather than zeroing was that zeroing lets the target learn a new solution), the recurrence is that **any intervention strong enough to make a model legible is strong enough to make it a different model, and the only tests that separate explanation from re-description are the ones scored against the pre-intervention behaviour.** Mechanical rule for us: **whenever we make anything trainable in order to make it readable - an adapter, a transcoder, an interpretable bottleneck, a probe fitted on a re-expressed activation - the claim ships with a matched test against the untouched weights, and that test is the model's own error predictions, not KL alone; a KL of 0.2 nats can coexist with a circuit that has quietly become the explanation of a different network.**
- **Pattern:** **The verification ladder in this entry is the most directly reusable artefact for our own evaluation design, because it says exactly where each question becomes answerable and why the thresholds are what they are: subset enumeration over all 2^k circuits is practical to k <= 13 (5,952 masked circuits), unusable by k = 17, and every matched frozen circuit sits above the limit (smallest 68 edges, median 416); per-edge necessity needs k <= 8 to be total (100% of edges individually necessary at <= 8 edges against a 2.5-15% median across tasks and 0.0% for matched frozen circuits); and the pair test scales as k(k-1)/2, which is why the 169,476 ablations only became affordable after condensation.** The pair test is also what produced the entry's strongest negative result: independence of edge effects failed in every circuit tested, with a median 7.4 interacting partners per edge and 87% of the strongest interactions sub-additive, so a circuit can be mapped completely and still not be readable one edge at a time. Read against run 754 (per-layer topology as the reusable summary, and the warning that a component story built on one checkpoint cannot separate mechanism from layer-index accident) and run 755 (a per-unit denominator dissolving a headline), the recurrence is that **the granularity at which a claim is checkable is a property of set size, not of the method, and a claim that was only sampled must be labelled as a sample.** Mechanical rule for us: **every interpretability claim we emit states its exhaustive limit - the k at which we enumerated every subset, the k at which necessity is total, the number of pairs actually run against the number implied - because "no smaller circuit suffices" and "no smaller circuit we sampled sufficed" are different sentences and only one of them is worth a theorem.**

- **Pattern:** **The estimator critique here is cheap and transferable, and it is about *where you evaluate the gradient* rather than about what you measure: integrating along a model-independent straight line from the clean to the corrupted activation spends most samples where the loss is flat, and the fix is to bend the path with one gradient step per sample toward the corrupted prediction.** The paper states the consequence for us directly - the number of steps is its only hyperparameter, `T = 1` collapses to plain EAP and `T = 2` to averaging the clean and corrupted gradients, so the sweep is a continuum from the old method to the new one rather than a replacement, and more steps can *degrade* the result once the normalised step size grows in a region where directions are unstable. Read against run 758 (a residual read at the wrong measurement point correlating at −0.05 while the MLP end of the same block correlated at −0.21) and run 759 (a dormancy rule that failed on one model because a structural assumption was smuggled into a cheap statistic), the recurrence is that **where in the computation and where along the interpolation you read the gradient decides the sign and size of the answer more than the reading method does**. Mechanical rule for us: **any attribution we publish states its interpolation path, its sample count per path, and whether a one-step and a two-step version of the same score were run as controls - because otherwise a null result is indistinguishable from a path that never left the flat region.**

- **Pattern:** **The losing definition here fails for a locatable reason and not for noise, and the reason is a structural assumption smuggled into a cheap statistic: "dormant" defined as high average attention to position zero presumes the sink sits at position zero, so on OLMo-2-1124-7B - which splits attention between two sinks, the second at an intermediate position - it identifies 0.0% of heads at every budget on every task, including GSM8K, while the output-norm rule reaches 1.8/14.5/16.0%.** Read against run 758 (an ablation read at two measurement points inside one block correlating at −0.05 and −0.21, so the residual was the wrong place to read the write) and run 755 (a dual head set whose 4.8-6.4x aggregate differential vanished per unit), the recurrence is that **every cheap statistic in this folder encodes an unstated assumption about where the interesting quantity lives, and the assumption is invisible until a model violates it.** Mechanical rule for us: **for every structural statistic we use to select units we state the invariant it presumes (fixed sink position, monotone depth, layer-uniform scale, single-corpus stationarity) and we test it on the one model in our panel most likely to violate it before it is allowed to select anything - because a selection rule that returns an empty set on one model is not a weak signal, it is a false premise, and the diagnostic is a single per-model null-return check that costs one forward pass.** The layer-relative normalisation is the transferable fix: dividing a unit's statistic by the mean over its own layer is what let one threshold array work across 28-48 layer networks.
- **Pattern:** **This is the folder's sharpest evidence that "unimportant" is a per-input selection and not a property of a unit - the same head is dormant on one question and active on the next, the set is re-chosen every forward pass, and the aggregate accuracy table hides a per-head dormancy spectrum that is bimodal: 64-82% of heads are dormant on at most 3% of MMLU questions, 46 of Llama-3.1-8B's 1,024 heads on at least 95% of them, and almost none (12 in Qwen2.5-14B, 0-1 in the other five) on all 14,042.** The paper is honest about the consequence it cannot buy: the rule cannot be turned into a static pruned model, and it says so before an efficiency reader can file it as a pruning paper. Read against run 757 (a beneficial-ablation set frozen on a disjoint discovery split, which is the same selection made *once*, offline, and averaged) and run 758 (importance estimated by repeated random joint ablation, 3,000 trials, one ranking per task), the distinction is that those entries estimate a corpus-level average and treat it as the unit's importance, while this one measures how much that average is a compromise - a head dormant on 95% of inputs contributes ~5% of a signal to the aggregate and is effectively invisible. Mechanical rule for us: **every unit-importance number we publish is accompanied by its input-conditional distribution - the fraction of inputs on which the unit is inert, the fraction on which it is load-bearing, and whether that distribution is bimodal - because a mean ablation delta over a corpus is a frequency-weighted blend of two populations, and the population a white-box model must predict on the next input is not the blend.** This is also why the random control here has to be size-matched *per input*: an across-corpus control zeroes a fixed random set and is not a fair null for a per-input rule.
- **Pattern:** **Two cheap checks in the appendix are worth stealing outright because each turns a plausible worry into a measured non-issue in one forward pass: dormancy rates are re-measured inside the modified model and are unchanged by the intervention (so the fixpoint problem - zeroing heads in layer 6 changes what downstream layers look dormant - does not arise), and the ablation is re-run with Gaussian noise matched to each head's own mean and standard deviation instead of zero, which preserves accuracy for a smaller fraction of heads (over 11% of Llama-3.2-3B's heads at the 0.5% budget).** The second result bounds the first from below: zeroing is not merely "a small perturbation", it is the *right-shaped* one, because head outputs are approximately zero-mean - so "these heads can be deleted for free" is true under a specific replacement value and materially weaker under a distribution-preserving one. Read against run 754 (the paper's own justification for refusing zero and mean ablation because they shift the input distribution) and run 752 (an intervention parameterised as a signed dose in the pair's own units, so the ablation value is on a scale the data chose), the recurrence is that **the ablation value is part of the estimand and the cheapest robustness test is a second replacement value on the same set.** Mechanical rule for us: **every "removable" set we report carries a second-arm replacement (matched-noise, or mean over a held-out corpus) and the fraction removable is reported for both - because a cell that survives zeroing and not a matched-noise swap is measuring the zero, and a cell that survives both is measuring the head.**

- **Pattern:** **This is the folder's first entry where the same intervention is read at two measurement points inside one block, and the two readings disagree by a factor of four - the ablation-induced representational change correlates with head-importance rank at -0.05 after the attention residual and -0.21 after the MLP - which converts a null into a localisation: the residual made the attention write look flat, and the MLP is where the write is actually consumed.** Read against run 750 (an aggregate loss delta at z +1.95 next to a target logit at z -52.5, diagnosed as downstream redundancy) and run 755 (a dual head set whose 4.8-6.4x aggregate differential vanishes per unit), the recurrence is that **where you read an intervention decides what it appears to do, and the residual stream is the worst place to read it.** Mechanical rule for us: **every intervention we score carries its measurement point named explicitly, and for any target quantity read off the residual stream we also read the same quantity after the next sublayer in the same block before concluding the effect is weak - because a residual add is a running sum, an effect that is flat there may merely have been added to something larger, and the before/after pair inside one block is the cheapest localisation available (no extra forward passes, one hook in, one hook out).**
- **Pattern:** **The sign-flipped ranking here is produced by a *different property*, not by a joint ablation, which is the cleanest contrast to run 757's beneficial-ablation result: cumulatively ablating the most spatially local 25% of heads first costs 43.6 points on Action against 34.3 for the top 25% by importance, quartile cross-tabs show the two orderings pick largely different heads, and the mechanism is attributed rather than assumed - fixed spatiotemporal kernels restore 56% of the local-set loss versus 27% of the importance-set loss, so much of what local heads do is a static stencil, not input-dependent routing.** Read against run 757 (a signed beneficial-ablation result whose sign the theory derives from conflicting objectives) and run 756 (a zero-before-output-projection ablation that finds a set whose removal *improves* held-out accuracy), the distinction is that those entries get negative and positive deltas for the *same* ranking under different seeds, while this one gets a larger positive-importance delta for a set chosen by an orthogonal statistic - so importance is not merely sign-ambiguous, it is not sufficient. Mechanical rule for us: **we keep at least one control ordering chosen by a property that is not the one we rank by (locality, distance, frequency, depth), and when that control out-damages our ranking we report the overlap between the two sets and a routing-only replacement test - because an importance score is a summary of one intervention family, and a set that loses more under cumulative ablation may be doing a simpler and more substitutable job than the mechanism we are looking for.**

- **Pattern:** **This is the folder's first signed beneficial-ablation result and it makes the point the whole ranking literature assumes away: the same screen produces a "task-critical" set when you look for damage and a "beneficial" set when you look for improvement, and neither is identified by effect size.** Every one of the twelve model-task pairs gains on held-out data once the subset is frozen on a disjoint discovery split (+13.10 points on SmolLM3 arithmetic, +6.30 on LLaMA arithmetic, ten pairs between +1.29 and +5.20), and the theory says why the sign can be negative at all: the shared coordinate's coefficient is pinned by the conflict, the optimum constrains only the *sum* w_j over heads, and GD's chosen decomposition puts that conflicted coordinate in one head - so deleting it is a positive move on the task that wanted it suppressed. Read against run 751 (a pattern with the opposite sign of causal effect, diagnosed as an interferer) and run 756 (a score family that must tie a dormant backup to an inert unit), the distinction is that run 751 documented a sign failure empirically and run 756 proved a ranking family blind, while this one gives a *generative account* of negative signs: they arise where two objectives disagree about one shared coordinate, not from noise. Mechanical rule for us: **every unit we call part of a mechanism carries a signed ablation delta per task, and a negative delta is reported as evidence that the objective conflicted rather than as an anomaly or a bad run - because the set that helps when removed and the set that hurts when removed are the same measurement with opposite signs, and a white-box model that predicts magnitude without sign cannot tell them apart.**
- **Pattern:** **The theoretical instrument is the deployment of a decomposition-of-the-optimum argument as a *null*, and it is cheap to reuse: the aggregate predictor is unique, the decomposition across heads is free, and the only thing that decides which decomposition training picks is the trajectory.** Proposition 4.1 does the first half in four lines of exact algebra (the model reduces to a linear predictor w^T x with w = sum over heads of o·v·tanh(qk), so the risks are quadratics in w and the joint optimum is (a/2, b, c)); Theorem 4.2 does the second half by showing small-initialisation GD makes one head per coordinate win with the losers at order α^4; Theorem 4.3 shows the consequence only fires on an event of probability 4/9. Read against run 750 (a proposal stage whose null passed while the verdict inverted) and run 753 (any fixed function of clean per-unit statistics ties a dormant unit to an inert one), the distinction is that those entries locate the blind spot in a *statistic*, while this one locates it in the gap between the optimum and the allocation - the loss landscape says nothing about which head holds what. Mechanical rule for us: **when we claim a weight-space statistic reveals a mechanism, we state the identification null explicitly - what the optimum pins (sums, aggregates) versus what it leaves free (allocation, decomposition) - and we treat the free part as the part that must be read from training dynamics or measured by intervention rather than inferred from the objective, because an optimum is a constraint on sums and a mechanism is a statement about terms.**

Read against run 755 (a headline dissolved by a per-unit denominator) and run 751 (a specificity ratio whose matched-random control was of the same order as the treated effect), the recurrence is that **a benchmark number is a joint statement about a method and its input, and the input is usually the part a reader assumes away.** Mechanical rule for us: **every score we publish is reported across a ladder of input qualities (oracle seed, method-derived seed, structure-free seed) with the ladder's worst rung stated in the abstract's terms, not buried - because the top rung measures the score and the bottom rung measures the pipeline anyone else would actually run, and where the bottom rung sits below the baseline we are claiming to beat, the contribution is the completion step and must be described as one.**
- **Pattern:** **The formal statement here is the second impossibility result in the folder and it is the sharpest kind - about a family of scores rather than a method, and it comes with the exact pair of objects that makes the claim testable: any score that is a fixed function of a unit's clean-state per-unit statistic must assign a dormant backup and an inert unit the same value, since both statistics vanish; the escaping construction is the growth in effect after the seed is already removed, which for a dormant unit reduces to the energy of its second-order coupling to the seed.** The paper then prices the ingredients and the price is lopsided - conditioning alone takes 0.33 to 0.80, centring against the output distribution takes it to 0.91, Fisher weighting adds 0.01 - and demonstrates the failure empirically with a synthetic benchmark where first-order energy *anti*-ranks 100 planted backups at 0.42. Mechanical rule for us: **we keep one statement per entry of the form "no score of shape X can separate A from B", and we pair it with the measured number that shows X is what people actually use - because an impossibility result with no baseline ladder under it is rhetoric, and an impossibility result with the ladder's 0.33-under-a-0.91-headline is an engineering spec.**

Read against run 752 (a dose axis showing a single deletion is one unmarked point on a curve) and run 748 (a capability measured under an intervention that the model had already compensated), the recurrence is that **an ablation result is an upper bound on a unit's importance whenever the model contains a substitute, and the bound is looser the more robust the circuit.** Mechanical rule for us: **before we report any knock-out number we report the knock-out of the primary alone, then the primary-plus-recovered-substitutes, then a size-matched set drawn from our own ranking - because the first number tells us the model repaired itself, the third tells us whether more removal is the whole story, and only the middle one is the circuit.**

- **Pattern:** **The comparison across unit classes here is honest in the way almost nothing else in this folder is: the method that wins on node sparsity prints its own loss on edge compression in the same appendix, with the number attached (93.73 / 94.69 / 99.21 percent against Edge Pruning's 94.77 / 98.88 / 98.75), and then shows the repair and prices it (about 3.7 and 3.6 further percentage points from post-hoc edge pruning, at +1.34 GB on IOI).** The deeper point is that the win is partly a statement about what the baselines *cannot express*: an edge mask over heads-and-blocks has no vocabulary for "this MLP block is gone", so 50-75% block-level MLP pruning was never on their table, and the paper is careful to report which of its gains are expressiveness and which are optimisation quality. Read against run 753 (a score family provably unable to separate dormant from absent) and run 744 (a rank-capped surrogate whose accuracy cost the headline omitted), the distinction is that those entries characterise a *method's* blind spot theoretically, while this one pays for its own blind spot in currency and repairs it in the appendix. Mechanical rule for us: **every claim that our reading is more compact / smaller / sparser than a baseline states which axes were unavailable to the baseline, and where a repair step exists we run it and print both the gain and its cost in the same table - because "we prune 50% of MLP blocks and they prune none" is partly a grammar difference, and the honest form of the number names the grammar.**
- **Pattern:** **The per-layer summaries are the single most reusable artefact in the entry and they say something the head-level literature cannot: the same three tasks yield three different *topologies*, and the topology is stable across model size — IOI is MLP-dominant with attention pruned in many layers (GPT-2 small keeps MLPs in 8 of 12 layers, Llama-3.1-8B the same shape across 32 layers), GP is localised and discontinuous (GPT-2 small keeps MLP computation in exactly layers 0, 3 and 7; Llama-3.2-1B in the first three layers), and GT is skip-like (a contiguous dead band in layers 2-5 of GPT-2 small, all attention in four layers of GPT-2-XL, each holding all 25 heads).** The GT case is the sharpest: the circuit is not "small" in a diffuse way but concentrated at a handful of depths with a hole in between, which is a prediction about *which* layers a white-box model must read for a numerical-comparison task and which it can skip. Read against run 751 (cross-architecture divergence in composed tasks, dense versus MoE) and run 748 (a MoE whose expert categories simply are not routed), the recurrence is that **where computation lives is a per-task fact first and a per-architecture fact second.** Mechanical rule for us: **for each behaviour we model we publish a per-layer occupancy profile — which depths carry the effect, which depths are dead — before any claim about which components implement it, and we compare the profile across at least two model sizes of the same family - because a component-level story built on one checkpoint cannot distinguish a mechanism from a layer-index accident, and a dead band is as informative as a live block.**
- **Pattern:** **The method's own justification for not ablating to zero is the folder's clearest statement of the compensation objection, and it is worth taking as a standing warning: zero and mean ablation shift the input distribution, so a pruning procedure optimising under them can learn a *new* solution (the authors cite lottery-ticket results) rather than isolate the mechanism, which is why every mask here interpolates toward an actively corrupted stream that flips the answer instead.** That is the right instinct, and it is also precisely the definition that makes the neuron-level claim narrower than it reads: a unit survives if swapping it to its corrupted value breaks the clean-versus-corrupted margin, so "many neurons coarse methods keep are irrelevant" is true *under adversarial interpolation* and says nothing about a neuron that matters under dose (run 752) or that is a dormant backup (run 753). The Llama fidelity row set confirms the tension from the other side: pruning *more* at 8B than at 1B (75% of blocks and 95.7% of heads on GP) at accuracy 0.99 and KL 0.23 is consistent with redundancy growing with scale and equally consistent with the corrupted stream doing more of the work. Mechanical rule for us: **we name the ablation value in every circuit claim and we do not transfer a sufficiency result from one ablation value to another - a unit shown causally necessary under corruption-flip interpolation is re-tested under dose or mean before we call it part of the mechanism, because the intervention defines the estimand and a different intervention asks a different question.**

- **Pattern:** **This is the first entry in the folder with a formal impossibility statement about a *class* of scores rather than about a particular method, and the statement is what makes the benchmark design non-arbitrary: any score that is a fixed function of a unit's clean-state per-unit statistics must assign a dormant backup and an inert unit the same value, because both statistics vanish for a unit that does nothing on the intact model.** The construction that escapes it is minimal - condition on the already-removed set and read the *growth* in effect - and the component ablation prices each ingredient: conditioning alone takes 0.33 to 0.80, centring against the output distribution takes it to 0.91, Fisher weighting adds 0.01. Mechanical rule for us: **before we publish any unit-importance score, we check whether it is a fixed function of intact-model per-unit statistics - if it is, we state that it cannot separate a component that is dormant from one that is absent, and we report the conditional (post-removal) counterpart alongside it - because "this unit does nothing on the clean model" is evidence for two mutually exclusive stories and no clean-pass number can tell them apart.**

- **Pattern:** **This is the folder's first entry that treats an intervention as an instrument with a calibration curve, and the calibration is the finding: a single deletion is one unmarked point on an axis whose scale the data, not the experimenter, chooses, so "the model repaired itself" and "the downstream unit always opposed the upstream one" are indistinguishable without the axis.** The construction is the one to steal - the arm is a clamp to a signed dose in units of the pair's own class contrast (+1 clean, 0 class-neutral midpoint, -1 full swap), the measurement is a second patch applied *inside* the dosed world so the primary's own shift cancels, and the estimand is the margin erased by the downstream override. On that axis 68 of 81 reachable directions are affine with a stable slope, 52 counterweights to 16 relays, and the crossing dose at which each flips sign is a fitted number rather than a story. Read against run 751 (a screen returning the correct-looking pattern with the *opposite* sign of causal effect) and run 750 (a proposal stage passing its null while the verdict inverted), the distinction is that those entries had a sign but no scale, while this one has a scale and reads the sign off it: run 751's interferers and this paper's counterweights are the same phenomenon seen through different instruments, and only the dose-resolved one says *how much* upstream signal reaches the verdict through that unit. Mechanical rule for us: **every intervention we publish is parameterised by a dose with a named unit (the model's own item contrast, not a global constant), the reported effect is a curve rather than a point, and every ablation-style claim carries the crossing dose at which the unit's sign flips - because a unit that opposes at rest and a unit that switches on under damage produce the identical single-point reading, and the curve is the only thing that separates them.**
- **Pattern:** **The competing explanation here is a pass-through multiplier, and the reason it loses is the dose *profile* rather than the magnitude - which gives us the sharpest null design in the folder so far.** The authors name final-normalisation renormalisation as the rival account, derive what it strictly predicts (a positive scalar cannot change a sign, so a dismissed direction can never become a two-sided contributor; amplification on an opposed direction predicts the *wrong* sign of recruitment; the gain-attributable share is bounded by |1-g|*|E0|), and then measure the gain per family, per class, per dose. The refutation is three-layered and each layer alone would be weak: the gain is dose-flat exactly where it is largest (Gemma's fake side, 1.080 to 1.103 across the sweep, while the unit's effect rises 4.5x), it moves the wrong way on true statements in both joint-core families (down to 0.926 and 0.890), it has the wrong predicted sign in half the audited cells, and where the sign is right it accounts for at most 4.5% of the observed recruitment (0.6% at the on-manifold dose). The paper also states where the null *would* win: deletion-type interventions sit in the shrinking regime where the mediator is real, so the audit explicitly does not transfer to zero/mean/resample ablation and a frozen-denominator control is retained for any such variant. Read against run 748 (a suppression table whose null read exactly 0.000 in two of four categories) and run 738 (a norm gap manufactured by a term in the loss), the recurrence is that **a confound is usually a multiplicative pass-through, and a multiplicative pass-through can counterfeit a small effect but cannot counterfeit a graded one.** Mechanical rule for us: **for every effect we report, we name the multiplicative mediators between the write and the readout (normalisation gain, soft-capping, temperature), derive the predictor's testable *signature* - not just its direction - and test the signature across the sweep; a null that is right in sign but flat where the effect is graded, or bounded at a few percent of it, is excluded and the exclusion is printed - because "the confound is small" is a weaker and harder claim than "the confound's signature is absent".**

Mechanical rule for us: **before we promise that a white-box reading of our network is exact or minimal, we name the structural assumption that licenses it (additivity, bounded scope, sparse interaction graph), state whether our model satisfies it, and say what the guarantee degrades to when it does not — because "we can compute the minimal explanation" is a theorem about the architecture, and the architecture is the thing we chose.**
